definition_zh: 公民身份；国籍；公民的权利与义务；公民品德；市民归属感
definition_en: the legal status of being a member of a state, together with its rights and duties, or the practice of taking part responsibly in a community
core_image: 桌上一本深色封面的小册子，写明一个人的名字与一串权利，旁边放着一张必须由本人去投的选票
scene: 入籍仪式的大厅里，一排人举右手跟着念誓词，桌上摊开一本深色封面的小册。After ten years in the country, she finally took the oath of citizenship.
sceneCN: 入籍仪式的大厅里，一排人举右手跟着念誓词，桌上摊开一本深色封面的小册；句中这个词指「依法取得的国家成员身份」（第 1 个义项：个人与国家之间的法定成员关系，附带权利与义务）。句意为她在这个国家住满十年后，终于宣誓取得公民身份。可辨识物件：誓词卡、举起的右手、深色小册、桌上的旗。

pos.zh: 公民身份；国籍（不可数）
公民品德；公民意识（不可数）
市民身份；对城镇的归属（不可数，较早的用法）

forms.label: 复数（指不同种类的身份）

senses.title: Legal membership of a state
senses.titleCN: 依法属于某个国家的成员身份
senses.definition: the legal status of belonging to a country, which brings a passport, protection and a permanent right to return
senses.definitionCN: 依法属于某个国家的身份，附带护照、领事保护与永久回国权
senses.example: After ten years in the country, she finally took the oath of citizenship.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这个国家住满十年后，终于宣誓取得公民身份。
senses.why: The native suffix -ship turns a person-word into a state-word, exactly as friend becomes friendship, so citizenship is the condition of being a citizen.
senses.whyCN: 本族后缀 -ship 把「人」变成「状态」，正如 friend 变 friendship，因此这个词就是「作为公民的状态」。

senses.title: The rights and duties that come with it
senses.titleCN: 随身份而来的权利与义务
senses.definition: the whole bundle of voting, taxation, obedience to law and claim on public services attached to membership
senses.definitionCN: 与成员身份相连的一整套权利与义务：投票、纳税、守法以及享有公共服务
senses.example: Citizenship brings the duty to pay tax as well as the right to vote.
senses.exampleCN: 公民身份既带来投票权，也带来纳税的义务。
senses.why: A status is not a badge but a two-sided contract, and English uses the same noun for both sides of it.
senses.whyCN: 这种身份不是一枚徽章，而是一份双面契约，英语用同一个名词同时指这两面。

senses.title: Taking part in public life
senses.definition: the practice of joining public decisions and shared work rather than only holding the paper
senses.definitionCN: 参与公共决策与共同事务的实际行动，而不只是持有一纸身份
senses.example: For her, citizenship meant showing up at council meetings, not just carrying a passport.
senses.exampleCN: 对她来说，公民身份意味着出席市政会议，而不只是带着一本护照。
senses.why: The noun was stretched from the legal tie to the activity that keeps the tie alive, because a right that nobody uses slowly disappears.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法律纽带扩展到维持纽带的行动，因为无人行使的权利会慢慢消失。

senses.title: Good conduct as a member
senses.definition: the quality of behaving responsibly toward neighbours and shared places
senses.definitionCN: 对邻里与公共空间负责任地行事的品质
senses.example: The school praised his citizenship after he organised a clean-up of the riverbank.
senses.exampleCN: 他组织了一次河岸清理，学校称赞了他的公民品德。
senses.why: -ship names a quality as well as a status, so the word can mean the virtue of a good member and not only the fact of membership.
senses.whyCN: -ship 既能指状态，也能指品质，因此这个词可指好成员的德行，而不只是成员这一事实。

senses.title: The school subject
senses.definition: a school subject that teaches how laws, elections and public services work
senses.definitionCN: 一门讲解法律、选举与公共服务如何运作的学校课程
senses.example: Citizenship is taught in year nine alongside history and geography.
senses.exampleCN: 九年级与历史、地理并行开设公民课。
senses.why: Modern curricula turned an abstract idea into a named subject, and the subject kept the plain noun rather than inventing a new one.
senses.whyCN: 现代课程把一个抽象理念变成有名目的科目，而这个科目沿用了朴素的原名词，没有另造新词。

senses.title: Corporate citizenship
senses.definition: the idea that a company owes duties to the society it operates in
senses.definitionCN: 认为企业对其所在社会负有责任的主张
senses.example: The bank advertises its corporate citizenship in every annual report.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行在每份年报里宣传自己的企业公民责任。
senses.why: The metaphor treats a company as a member with duties, which lets moral language be applied to a firm.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把公司当作负有责任的成员，从而把道德语言用到企业身上。

senses.title: Global citizenship
senses.definition: a sense of belonging to humanity as a whole rather than to one state
senses.definitionCN: 认为自己属于全人类而非某一国家的归属感
senses.example: Climate campaigns appeal to global citizenship rather than to national loyalty.
senses.exampleCN: 气候运动诉诸世界公民意识，而不是国家忠诚。
senses.why: The same membership idea is stretched to a borderless community, and the stretch is marked by the adjective global.
senses.whyCN: 同一个成员身份观念被拉伸到一个没有国界的共同体，global 这个形容词标出了这一拉伸。

senses.title: Belonging to a town
senses.definition: membership in a town or neighbourhood, shown by daily involvement rather than by papers
senses.definitionCN: 对城镇或街区的成员感，靠日常参与而非证件来体现
senses.example: Her citizenship of the old quarter was a matter of daily errands, not papers.
senses.exampleCN: 她对老城区的归属感体现在每天的琐事里，而不是证件上。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is the city: Latin civitas named the body of townspeople before it named a state.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层是「城市」：拉丁语 civitas 先指城镇居民全体，后来才指国家。

intro.en: Citizenship is citizen plus the native suffix -ship, which turns a person into a state or a quality. Citizen itself reaches English through Old French from Latin civitas 'the body of citizens', built on civis 'citizen'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: citizenship 由 citizen 加本族后缀 -ship 构成，这个后缀把「人」变成「状态」或「品质」。citizen 本身经古法语来自拉丁 civitas「公民全体」，其词根为 civis「公民」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Civis meant 'citizen, townsman'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link sometimes proposed to a root meaning 'to settle' remains a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: civis 意为「公民、城里人」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人提出的与「定居」词根的联系仍属假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Civitas first named the condition of being a citizen, then the whole body of citizens and their commonwealth; the abstract and the collective readings existed side by side.
items.cn: civitas 先指「身为公民的状态」，再指「公民全体及其共同体」；抽象义与集合义长期并存。

items.en: Old French cité came from civitas but narrowed to 'city, town', losing the political sense. English city follows this line, which is why city and citizen look alike but name different things.
items.cn: 古法语 cité 出自 civitas，却收窄为「城市、城镇」，丢掉了政治含义。英语 city 沿这条线发展，所以 city 与 citizen 形近却指不同事物。

items.en: The person-word entered English around 1300 as citisein, 'inhabitant of a city'. The older English word for a townsman was burgess, and citizen gradually replaced it.
items.cn: 指人的这个词约在 1300 年以 citisein 进入英语，意为「城市居民」。英语里更早表示市民的词是 burgess，citizen 逐渐取代了它。

items.en: The native suffix -ship, historically related to shape, first named a condition or an office, as in friendship and lordship. From the sixteenth century it formed citizenship, 'the state of being a citizen'.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -ship 在历史上与 shape 相关，先表示「状态」或「职位」，如 friendship 与 lordship。到十六世纪构成 citizenship，即「身为公民的状态」。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word also named school instruction and good conduct; the corporate and global uses are twentieth-century extensions. Source uncertain (first date): no exact first citation is recorded for either extension.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词也指学校课程与端正品行；企业义与世界公民义是二十世纪的扩展。首见年代不确定：这两种扩展都没有确切的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin civis stock, easy to confuse at sight; group two holds near neighbours that also name a tie between a person and a state or place.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 civis 词族、容易看错的词；第二组是同样表示「人与国家或地方的联系」的近义词。

entries.definition: The countable person-word: one who holds the status. Citizenship is the status itself and cannot be counted the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 可数的「人」：持有该身份的个人。citizenship 是身份本身，不能同样计数。

entries.definition: A large town. It comes from the same Latin source but through a branch that narrowed to the place, so it never means a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指大城市。同出拉丁来源，但走的是收窄为「地方」的那条支线，因此从不指人。

entries.definition: The adjective for things belonging to a town or to citizens' duties. It describes the field, while citizenship names the status.
entries.definitionCN: 指「属于城镇或公民义务」的形容词，描述领域，而 citizenship 指身份本身。

entries.definition: A society and its culture at a developed stage. The ending -ization names a process, not a membership, and the word is not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指发展到较高阶段的社会及其文化。-ization 结尾表示过程，而非成员身份，二者并非同义。

entries.definition: The legal tie to a state, often used when passports and immigration are discussed; it stresses the state's side, while citizenship stresses the member's rights and duties.
entries.definitionCN: 与国家之间的法律纽带，常用于护照与移民语境；它强调国家一侧，而 citizenship 强调成员的权利与义务。

entries.definition: The right to live in a country without full political membership; a resident may pay tax and still be unable to vote.
entries.definitionCN: 在一国居住的权利，但不含完整政治成员身份；居民可能纳税却无法投票。

entries.definition: The condition of being a subject of a crown rather than a citizen of a republic; the duties run upward to a ruler.
entries.definitionCN: 指身为君主臣民而非共和国公民的状态；义务朝上指向统治者。

entries.definition: The official process by which a foreigner acquires citizenship; it names the step, not the resulting status.
entries.definitionCN: 外国人取得公民身份的官方程序；它指这一步过程，而非取得后的身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real native suffix, a real Latin root and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的本族后缀、真实的拉丁词根与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: -ship turns a person into a condition: citizen gives citizenship, friend gives friendship.
normal.cn: -ship 把「人」变成「状态」：citizen 得 citizenship，friend 得 friendship。

normal.en: The family runs citizen, citizenship, city, civic, civil and civilian.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 citizen、citizenship、city、civic、civil 与 civilian。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the legal field: grant citizenship, dual citizenship, citizenship ceremony.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律领域：授予公民身份、双重国籍、入籍仪式。

normal.en: Latin civis also lies inside civitas, the source of both city and citizen.
normal.cn: 拉丁 civis 也在 civitas 之中，而 civitas 同时是 city 与 citizen 的来源。

normal.en: The word always pairs a right with a duty: the vote and the tax return.
normal.cn: 这个词总把权利与义务配成一对：选票与报税单。

abstract.en: Picture a key that opens a town hall but carries a list of chores on the same ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能打开市政厅的钥匙，钥匙圈上同时挂着一串必须完成的杂事。

abstract.en: Picture a membership card that grows warmer the more often it is used.
abstract.cn: 想象一张会员卡，用得越频繁，摸起来越温热。

abstract.en: Picture a passport that is also a rota, saying when you must show up.
abstract.cn: 想象一本护照同时是一张值班表，写明你何时必须到场。

examples.en: Dual citizenship forced him to choose which passport to renew.
examples.cn: 双重国籍逼他选择续办哪一本护照。

examples.en: The council treats clean streets as a test of citizenship.
examples.cn: 市政会把街道整洁当作公民意识的一种检验。

examples.en: Citizenship classes cover voting, taxation and local services.
examples.cn: 公民课涵盖投票、纳税与地方公共服务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「公民」加「船」：同坐一条船的人，才有身份、权利与义务——注意这只是谐音联想，并非词源

root: 拉丁 civis「公民」→ civitas「公民身份、公民全体」→ 古法语 cité「城市」→ 中古英语 citisein「市民」；英语 citizen 加本族后缀 -ship（状态、身份）构成 citizenship。civis 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a paper to a practice: the legal status first, then the two sides of its contract, then participation, conduct, the school subject, the company, the planet and finally the old town.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一纸身份走向实际践行：先讲法定身份，再讲契约的两面，然后依次是参与、品行、学校科目、企业、全球，最后回到古老的城镇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded booklet that names one person as a member of a body, with rights printed on one page and duties on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本折起的小册子把一个人写进某个共同体，一页印权利，另一页印义务。

branches.en: The booklet is the legal tie, and the tie runs both ways: a passport on one page, a tax form on the other.
branches.cn: 小册子是法律纽带，而纽带走双向：一页是护照，另一页是报税表。

branches.en: Belonging is practised where one lives: council meetings in the present, the old quarter in the past.
branches.cn: 归属在日常所在地被实践：当下的市政会议，以及过去的老城区。

branches.en: Conduct becomes teachable: the virtue of a good member is turned into a school subject with a syllabus.
branches.cn: 品行变成可教之物：好成员的德行被整理成有教学大纲的一门课。

branches.en: The metaphor makes a firm a member, so that moral duties can be asked of a company.
branches.cn: 比喻把企业当作成员，于是可以向公司追问道德责任。

branches.en: The border of the body is removed, leaving humanity as the only remaining community.
branches.cn: 共同体的边界被撤掉，只剩全人类作为唯一剩下的社群。

intro.en: Citizenship is a native suffix laid on a borrowed noun, so the word can be read as one person-noun plus one state-suffix.
intro.cn: citizenship 是把本族后缀加在借来的名词上，因此可按「一个指人的名词＋一个表状态的后缀」来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the noun civis and its abstract civitas, but has no suffix matching -ship; the state-suffix is native English and historically related to shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供名词 civis 及其抽象形式 civitas，但没有与 -ship 对应的后缀；这个表状态的后缀是本族英语成分，历史上与 shape 相关。

items.example: Civis is the root that carries the idea of membership.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载「成员身份」的观念。

items.structure: civitas (Latin abstract noun, 'citizenship, body of citizens')
items.meaning: the condition of a citizen; the citizen body
items.example: Civitas adds the abstract ending to civis.
items.exampleCN: civitas 在 civis 上加了抽象后缀。

items.example: The place branch narrowed away from the political sense.
items.exampleCN: 指地方的这条支线从政治含义中收窄出来。

items.example: The suffix makes a status out of a person-noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把指人的名词变成一种身份。

items.meaning: a member of a city or state
items.example: The person-word entered English around 1300.
items.exampleCN: 这个指人的词约在 1300 年进入英语。

items.meaning: the status or virtue of a citizen
items.example: The suffix adds the abstract reading to the person-word.
items.exampleCN: 后缀为指人的词添上抽象含义。

items.meaning: belonging to a town or its citizens
items.example: The adjective describes the field rather than the person.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述领域，而非指人。

items.meaning: a person not in the armed forces
items.example: The word contrasts the private person with the uniformed state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词把私人身份的平民与穿制服的公权力对立起来。

items.meaning: the citizens taken as a group
items.example: The collective suffix gathers many holders of the status.
items.exampleCN: 集合后缀把许多持有该身份的人聚为一体。

latinEntries.structure: civicus, civica, civicum (adjective, first and second declension)

derivatives.zh: 非公民；不具有该国国籍的人

definition_zh: 公民；市民；城镇居民；（某地的）居民；有公共意识的普通人
definition_en: a person who legally belongs to a state and holds its rights, or an inhabitant of a city or town
core_image: 一个普通人站在市政厅门口，手里拿着一张写满权利与义务的卡片，脚边是他每天走过的街道
scene: 市政厅的公开听证会上，一位普通居民站起来，要求查看预算的每一行。Any citizen may inspect the council's spending records.
sceneCN: 市政厅的公开听证会上，一位普通居民站起来，要求查看预算的每一行；句中这个词指「依法属于某国并享有该国权利的人」（第 1 个义项：以出生或授予方式取得某国法定成员身份的个人）。句意为任何公民都可以查阅市政会的支出记录。可辨识物件：听证席、预算表、麦克风、旁听席。

pos.zh: 公民；国民（可数）
市民；城镇居民（可数）
（某地的）居民；常客（可数，较随意）

senses.title: Legal member of a state
senses.titleCN: 依法属于某个国家的成员
senses.definition: a person who is a legal member of a country, by birth or by grant, and who holds its passport and protection
senses.definitionCN: 以出生或授予方式成为某国法定成员的人，持有该国护照并受其保护
senses.example: Any citizen may inspect the council's spending records.
senses.exampleCN: 任何公民都可以查阅市政会的支出记录。
senses.why: Latin civis named the member of a citizen body, and English kept that person-word while the abstract status became citizenship.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 civis 指公民全体中的一员，英语保留了这一指人的词，而抽象身份另由 citizenship 承担。

senses.title: Inhabitant of a town
senses.definition: a person who lives in a particular city or town, whether or not the state is mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 住在某个城市或城镇的人，不论是否涉及国家层面
senses.example: The citizens of the old town fought to keep the market square open.
senses.exampleCN: 老城的居民力争保住那片开放的集市广场。
senses.why: The word entered English as 'townsman' long before it meant 'member of a state', and that local reading never disappeared.
senses.whyCN: 这个词以「城里人」之义进入英语，远早于「国家成员」义，而地方义从未消失。

senses.title: Holder of political rights
senses.definition: a person entitled to vote, petition the government and stand for public office
senses.definitionCN: 有权投票、向政府请愿并竞选公职的人
senses.example: Only citizens could vote in the referendum.
senses.exampleCN: 只有公民才能在全民公投中投票。
senses.why: Rights are the practical content of membership, so the person-word is used whenever those rights are exercised.
senses.whyCN: 权利是成员身份的实际内容，因此只要行使这些权利，就会用到这个指人的词。

senses.title: Engaged member of a community
senses.titleCN: 积极参与共同体事务的人
senses.definition: a person who takes part in public life and looks after shared places
senses.definitionCN: 参与公共生活、照看共享空间的人
senses.example: She is a citizen of her neighbourhood before she is a subject of the state.
senses.exampleCN: 她先是自己街区的成员，然后才是国家的臣民。
senses.why: The virtue of citizenship needs a human carrier, and the person-word supplies that carrier.
senses.whyCN: 公民品德需要人的载体，而这个指人的词正好提供了这个载体。

senses.title: Ordinary person, not an official
senses.definition: an ordinary member of the public, as opposed to a soldier, police officer or official
senses.definitionCN: 与军人、警察或官员相对的普通公众成员
senses.example: The inquiry heard from soldiers and citizens alike.
senses.exampleCN: 调查听取了军人和平民双方的说法。
senses.why: The old contrast between the uniformed state and the private person gave the word this plain, unglamorous sense.
senses.whyCN: 穿制服的公权力与私人个体之间的古老对照，给了这个词这种朴素、不起眼的含义。

senses.title: Volunteer in research
senses.titleCN: 参与科研的公众志愿者
senses.definition: a member of the public who collects observations or data for a research project
senses.definitionCN: 为研究项目收集观察或数据的普通公众成员
senses.example: Hundreds of citizens logged the birds they saw that weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 那个周末有数百名公众记录了他们看到的鸟。
senses.why: Modern compounds borrow the word for unpaid public help, because the helper is a member of the community rather than an employee.
senses.whyCN: 现代复合词借这个词表示无偿的公众协助，因为协助者是共同体成员，而非雇员。

senses.title: Citizen of the world
senses.definition: a person who feels loyalty to humanity rather than to a single nation
senses.definitionCN: 把忠诚献给全人类而非单一国家的人
senses.example: He called himself a citizen of the world and kept three passports.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称世界公民，并持三本护照。
senses.why: The metaphor extends membership past the state border, leaving the person-word with a wider body to belong to.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把成员身份延伸到国界之外，使这个指人的词归属于一个更大的共同体。

senses.title: Freeman of a borough
senses.titleCN: 享有特权的市镇自由民
senses.definition: historically, a freeman of a borough with the right to trade and vote there
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指享有在该市镇经商与投票权利的自由民
senses.example: The guild admitted citizens of the borough, not outsiders.
senses.exampleCN: 行会只接纳本自治市的自由民，不接纳外来者。
senses.why: The medieval town meaning survives in civic titles and in the phrase freeman of the borough, where citizen is a privilege and not a nationality.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的市镇义仍留在市政头衔与「市镇自由民」这一说法里，那里的公民是一种特权，而非国籍。

intro.en: Citizen comes from Anglo-French citesein and Old French citeien, 'inhabitant of a city', built on cité 'city' from Latin civitas. The word widened from townsman to member of a state in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: citizen 来自盎格鲁-法语 citesein 与古法语 citeien「城市居民」，其基础是出自拉丁 civitas 的 cité「城市」。十六世纪这个词从「市民」扩展为「国家成员」。

items.en: Civis meant 'citizen, townsman'. Its deeper origin is not established, and the connection sometimes drawn to a settling root is a hypothesis rather than a proven derivation.
items.cn: civis 意为「公民、城里人」。其更深来源未得到证明，有时与「定居」词根拉上的联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Civitas named both the condition of a citizen and the whole body of citizens, so the abstract and collective readings were present from the start.
items.cn: civitas 既指「公民的状态」，也指「公民全体」，因此抽象义与集合义从一开始就同时存在。

items.en: Old French cité narrowed civitas to 'city, town', and the political sense was carried instead by the person-word. English city descends from this narrowed branch.
items.cn: 古法语 cité 把 civitas 收窄为「城市、城镇」，政治含义改由指人的词承担。英语 city 就出自这条收窄的支线。

items.en: Around 1300 English borrowed citesein 'inhabitant of a city'. It replaced the native burgess in many contexts, and for two centuries it meant townsman rather than national.
items.cn: 约 1300 年英语借入 citesein「城市居民」。它在许多语境中取代了本族的 burgess，并在两百年间指「市民」而非「国民」。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word was used for a member of a state with political rights, especially in contrast with subject and alien; this is the sense that now dominates.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词用于指享有政治权利的国家成员，尤其与「臣民」「外侨」相对；这一义项如今占主导。

items.en: The twentieth century produced citizen science, citizen journalism and citizen soldier, all naming an ordinary person who takes on a specialist role. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest citation of each compound is not fixed.
items.cn: 二十世纪产生了「公众科研」「公民新闻」「公民士兵」等说法，都指临时承担专业角色的普通人。首见年代不确定：各复合词的最早书证并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin civis stock that are easy to mistake for one another; group two holds words that also name a person tied to a state or place.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 civis 词族、容易互相看错的词；第二组是同样指「与国家或地方相连的个人」的词。

entries.definition: The abstract status held by a citizen. The person is a citizen; the paper or condition is citizenship.
entries.definitionCN: 公民持有的抽象身份。人本身是 citizen，而那纸身份或状态是 citizenship。

entries.definition: A large town, from the same Latin source but through the branch that named the place. A city contains citizens but is not one.
entries.definitionCN: 指大城市，同出拉丁来源，但走的是命名「地方」的支线。城市容纳公民，但城市本身不是公民。

entries.definition: The adjective of a town or of citizens' duties; it cannot stand alone for a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指城镇或公民义务的形容词，不能单独用来指人。

entries.definition: A person who is not in the armed forces. Every civilian is a citizen in the plain sense, but the word contrasts with soldier, not with foreigner.
entries.definitionCN: 指不在军队中的人。每个平民都是朴素意义上的公民，但这个词是与军人相对，而非与外国人相对。

entries.definition: Politeness in speech and manner. It shares the root but names conduct, not membership, and is not a synonym of citizen.
entries.definitionCN: 指言谈举止上的礼貌。它同根，却指行为而非成员身份，不是 citizen 的同义词。

entries.definition: A person who holds a country's nationality, especially in passport and immigration contexts; it names the legal tie more than the daily role.
entries.definitionCN: 指持有某国国籍的人，尤其用于护照与移民语境；它更强调法律纽带，而非日常角色。

entries.definition: A person under the rule of a monarch. A subject owes obedience upward, while a citizen holds rights against the state.
entries.definitionCN: 指君主统治下的人。臣民的义务朝上指向君主，而公民对国家持有权利。

entries.definition: A person who lives in a place, with or without political membership; a resident can be a foreign national.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某地居住的人，不论有无政治成员身份；居民可以是外国国民。

entries.definition: An informal word for a person from the area, with no legal weight at all; it marks familiarity with a place, not membership in a state.
entries.definitionCN: 口语里指本地人，完全没有法律分量；它标出对某地的熟悉，而非国家成员身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin root, a real Anglo-French borrowing and real compounds in current use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的盎格鲁-法语借词，以及仍在使用的真实复合词。

normal.en: Latin civis 'citizen' produces citizen, city, civic and civilian, all in one family.
normal.cn: 拉丁 civis「公民」衍生出 citizen、city、civic 与 civilian，同属一个词族。

normal.en: The word first meant townsman: a citizen was someone who belonged to a city before he belonged to a state.
normal.cn: 这个词最初指市民：公民先是属于一座城，然后才属于一个国家。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modern uses: senior citizen, citizen science, citizen journalism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出现代用法：长者、公众科研、公民新闻。

normal.en: The abstract noun is citizenship, formed with the native suffix -ship.
normal.cn: 抽象名词是 citizenship，由本族后缀 -ship 构成。

normal.en: Official forms ask for proof of citizenship, not proof of citizen.
normal.cn: 官方表格要求的是公民身份证明，而不是「公民本人」的证明。

abstract.en: Picture one face in a crowd that the town recognises by name.
abstract.cn: 想象人群中的一张脸，这座城能叫出他的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a key to the town hall that comes with a list of chores.
abstract.cn: 想象一把市政厅的钥匙，附带一张待办杂事清单。

abstract.en: Picture a passport that doubles as a library card for the whole world.
abstract.cn: 想象一本护照同时是全世界的借书证。

examples.en: Every citizen over eighteen may sign the petition.
examples.cn: 年满十八岁的每位公民都可签署这份请愿书。

examples.en: The citizens of the valley opposed the new dam.
examples.cn: 河谷的居民反对新建水坝。

examples.en: As a citizen of the world, she donated to relief funds on three continents.
examples.cn: 作为世界公民，她向三大洲的救济基金捐款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「city（城市）+ zen（禅）」——在城市里静心做事的人，就是市民；这只是谐音联想，并非词源

root: 拉丁 civis「公民」→ civitas「公民全体、公民身份」→ 古法语 cité「城市」→ 古法语 citeien／盎格鲁-法语 citesein「城市居民」→ 英语 citizen；十六世纪扩展为「国家成员」。civis 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person through widening circles: the state, the town, the voting booth, the neighbourhood, the crowd of ordinary people, the research project, the planet and finally the medieval borough.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个人穿过一圈圈扩大的范围：国家、城镇、投票站、街区、普通人群、研究项目、整个地球，最后回到中世纪的自治市镇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ordinary person standing at the door of a town hall, holding a card of rights in one hand and the street he walks every day under his feet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个普通人站在市政厅门口，一手拿着写有权利的卡片，脚下是他每天走过的街道。

branches.en: Membership becomes practical at the ballot box: the status turns into a hand that can vote and a voice that can petition.
branches.cn: 成员身份在投票站变得实际：身份化为一只可投票的手与一个可请愿的声音。

branches.en: The town is the older body: the resident of today continues the privileged freeman of the medieval borough.
branches.cn: 城镇是更古老的共同体：今天的居民延续了中世纪自治市镇里享有特权的自由民。

branches.en: Care for shared places widens outward until the neighbourhood and the planet are both claimed as home.
branches.cn: 对共享空间的照看向外扩展，直到街区与地球都被认作家园。

branches.en: Against the uniformed state stands the plain person, whose only badge is ordinary clothing.
branches.cn: 与穿制服的公权力相对的是朴素个人，他唯一的徽章就是平常衣着。

branches.en: The plain person is borrowed for research, doing a specialist's work without a specialist's title.
branches.cn: 朴素个人被借去参与研究，做专业工作却不带专业头衔。

intro.en: Citizen is a borrowed person-noun whose endings also build the abstract status, the collective body and the adjective of the town.
intro.cn: citizen 是借来的指人名词，它的各种词尾还构成抽象身份、集合群体与城镇形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin civis supplies the root, and civitas supplies the abstract and collective readings that English later split between city and citizenship.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 civis 提供词根，civitas 提供抽象义与集合义，英语后来把这二者分给 city 与 citizenship。

items.example: The root carries membership of a body of townspeople.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载「属于城镇居民全体」的意思。

items.example: The abstract ending turns the member into the whole body.
items.exampleCN: 抽象词尾把单个成员变成整个群体。

items.example: The place branch narrowed away from the political sense.
items.exampleCN: 指地方的支线从政治含义中收窄出来。

items.example: The person-noun is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个指人的名词是英语词的直接祖先。

items.meaning: a member of a town or state
items.example: English reshaped the ending into its own person pattern.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个词尾改造成自己的指人模式。

items.example: The native suffix builds citizenship from citizen.
items.exampleCN: 本族后缀由 citizen 构成 citizenship。

items.example: The adjective names the field rather than the person.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词命名领域，而不指人。

items.meaning: a person not in the armed forces
items.example: The word contrasts the plain person with the uniformed state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词把朴素个人与穿制服的公权力对立起来。

items.example: The collective ending gathers the holders of the status.
items.exampleCN: 集合词尾把持有该身份的人聚在一起。

latinEntries.structure: civicus, civica, civicum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 城市的；市政的；公民的；公民义务的；公民品德的
definition_en: relating to a city or town, or to the rights and duties of the people who belong to it
core_image: 一座石砌的市政厅立在广场一侧，台阶上贴着通知，市民从门前经过时抬头看那座钟
scene: 广场旁的老市场被改建成一座供市民集会、借书、听讲座的公共建筑。The old market hall was restored as a civic centre for the town.
sceneCN: 广场旁的老市场被改建成一座供市民集会、借书、听讲座的公共建筑；句中这个词指「属于城市公共事务的」（第 1 个义项：与城市或城镇作为公共共同体相关的）。句意为老市场被修复成镇上的市民活动中心。可辨识物件：石砌立面、公告栏、钟、台阶上的人。

pos.zh: 城市的；市政的
公民的；公民义务与权利的

derivatives.zh: 以公民身份；就市政而言

senses.title: Of a city as a place
senses.titleCN: 属于城市或城镇这个空间
senses.definition: relating to a city or town as a physical and social place
senses.definitionCN: 与城市或城镇作为实体与社会场所相关的
senses.example: The old market hall was restored as a civic centre for the town.
senses.exampleCN: 老市场被修复成镇上的市民活动中心。
senses.why: Latin civicus meant 'of a citizen', and English attached it first to the town that the citizens share.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 civicus 意为「公民的」，英语先把它附在公民共有的城镇上。

senses.title: Of municipal government
senses.definition: relating to the elected government and public services of a town
senses.definitionCN: 与城镇的民选政府及公共服务相关的
senses.example: The mayor opened the civic budget to public view.
senses.exampleCN: 市长把市政预算向公众公开。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the institution that runs the town, so civic means municipal as well as urban.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也附在管理城镇的机构上，因此既指「城市的」，也指「市政的」。

senses.title: Of a citizen's duties
senses.definition: relating to what people owe the community by virtue of belonging to it
senses.definitionCN: 与人们因属于共同体而对它应尽之事相关的
senses.example: Voting is treated as a civic duty, not a private hobby.
senses.exampleCN: 投票被视为公民义务，而不是私人爱好。
senses.why: The same adjective covers the member's side of the city, where belonging creates obligations.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词也覆盖成员这一侧，也就是归属产生义务的一面。

senses.title: Of a citizen's rights
senses.definition: relating to the rights people hold as members of a community
senses.definitionCN: 与人们作为共同体成员所持权利相关的
senses.example: The charter lists civic rights such as petition and assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 宪章列明请愿与集会等公民权利。
senses.why: Rights and duties are two faces of one membership, and English uses one adjective for both faces.
senses.whyCN: 权利与义务是同一成员身份的两面，英语用同一个形容词指这两面。

senses.title: Civic pride
senses.definition: a feeling of attachment to and satisfaction with one's town
senses.definitionCN: 对所在城镇的依恋与满意之情
senses.example: The clean square was a matter of civic pride.
senses.exampleCN: 广场保持整洁，是市民自豪感的一部分。
senses.why: Pride is the emotional form of belonging, so the adjective of the town also names a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 自豪是归属感的情感形态，因此城镇的形容词也用来指一种情感。

senses.title: Civic engagement
senses.definition: organized participation in public affairs, such as volunteering, campaigning or attending meetings
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地参与公共事务，如志愿服务、竞选活动或出席会议
senses.example: Civic engagement rose after the library began hosting debates.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆开始举办辩论会后，公民参与度上升了。
senses.why: Modern political language turns the adjective into a label for activity, and the label spreads through policy reports.
senses.whyCN: 现代政治语言把这个形容词变成活动的标签，这个标签又通过政策报告扩散开来。

senses.title: Civic education
senses.definition: instruction in how citizenship, laws and public institutions work
senses.definitionCN: 讲解公民身份、法律与公共机构如何运作的教育
senses.example: The school added a civic education module on local taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 学校增设了一个关于地方税收的公民教育单元。
senses.why: Curricula name the subject after the idea, so civic education sits beside history and geography.
senses.whyCN: 课程用这个理念给科目命名，于是公民教育与历史、地理并列。

senses.title: Civic style in building
senses.definition: the plain, monumental manner of buildings put up for public use
senses.definitionCN: 为公共用途而建的建筑所呈现的朴素、庄重风格
senses.example: The station was rebuilt in a plain civic style.
senses.exampleCN: 车站以朴素的市政风格重建。
senses.why: Buildings that serve the public are described by the public they serve, and the adjective becomes a style label.
senses.whyCN: 为公众服务的建筑，用它们所服务的公众来命名，这个形容词由此成为风格标签。

intro.en: Civic comes from French civique and Latin civicus 'of a citizen', built on civis 'citizen'. English took the adjective in the seventeenth century, later than it took the person-noun.
intro.cn: civic 来自法语 civique 与拉丁 civicus「公民的」，其词根为 civis「公民」。英语在十七世纪才借入这个形容词，晚于指人的名词。

items.en: Civis meant 'citizen, townsman'. Its deeper origin is not established; any older root offered for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: civis 意为「公民、城里人」。其更深来源未得到证明；为它给出的任何更早词根都是重构形式，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Civicus was the adjective 'of a citizen, of citizens'. Latin used it for the dress, the duty and the law of a citizen, so the word already carried both the town and the obligation.
items.cn: civicus 是形容词「公民的、属于公民的」。拉丁语用它指公民的衣着、义务与法律，因此这个词从一开始就同时带着「城市」与「义务」。

items.en: French civique continued the Latin adjective. It was used in political writing before English borrowed it, which is why the English word keeps a formal, civic tone.
items.cn: 法语 civique 延续了拉丁形容词。英语借入之前，它已用于政治写作，因此英语这个词带有正式、市政的语气。

items.en: English civic is recorded from the seventeenth century in the sense 'pertaining to a city or citizens'. The word entered through learned and political prose, not through everyday speech.
items.cn: 英语 civic 自十七世纪起有「属于城市或公民的」这一义项。这个词经学术与政治散文进入英语，而非通过日常口语。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the adjective formed civic duty, civic pride and civic rights; the policy compounds civic engagement and civic education are later still. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest citation of each compound is not fixed.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个形容词构成公民义务、市民自豪感与公民权利；政策用语中的公民参与、公民教育更晚。首见年代不确定：各复合词的最早书证并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the civis root or a very close spelling; group two holds adjectives that also describe public or town life.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 civis 词根或拼写极近的词；第二组是同样描述公共或城市生活的形容词。

entries.definition: From Latin civilis 'of a citizen', but it means polite, non-military or belonging to ordinary law. A civil war is not a civic event, and civil manners are not municipal services.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁 civilis「公民的」，但意为「有礼的、非军事的、属于民事法律的」。内战不是市政事件，礼貌也不是市政服务。

entries.definition: The person who holds citizenship; civic is only the adjective and never names a human being.
entries.definitionCN: 持有公民身份的人；civic 只是形容词，从不指人。

entries.definition: A person who is not a soldier. It shares the root but contrasts with military service, not with a town.
entries.definitionCN: 指不是军人的人。它同根，但对照的是军役，而非城市。

entries.definition: A large town; the noun names the place, while civic names what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指大城市；名词指地方，而 civic 指属于该地方的事物。

entries.definition: The plural-looking noun for the study of citizenship and government. It ends in -s but is singular in use.
entries.definitionCN: 这个看起来像复数的名词指对公民身份与政体的研究。词尾有 -s，实际作单数用。

entries.definition: Relating to the administration of a town, especially its council and services; narrower than civic, which also covers duties, pride and rights.
entries.definitionCN: 与城镇行政相关，尤其指市政会及其服务；比 civic 窄，civic 还涵盖义务、自豪感与权利。

entries.definition: Relating to a town as a built and populated area, in contrast with rural; it says nothing about citizenship or duties.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为建成并有人居住的区域的城市，与乡村相对；完全不涉及公民身份或义务。

entries.definition: Open to everyone or owned by the community; a public building may be civic in tone, but public stresses access rather than membership.
entries.definitionCN: 向所有人开放或由共同体所有；公共建筑可能带市政气息，但 public 强调的是可及性，而非成员身份。

entries.definition: Shared by a group of people, often a small community; it stresses common ownership, not a town's formal institutions.
entries.definitionCN: 由一群人共享，常指较小共同体；它强调共同所有，而非城镇的正式机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin adjective, a real French borrowing and real policy compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁形容词、真实的法语借词与真实的政策搭配。

normal.en: The root civis gives citizen, city, civic and civilian, one family with four faces.
normal.cn: 词根 civis 衍生出 citizen、city、civic 与 civilian，一个词族有四张面孔。

normal.en: The ending -ic means 'relating to', so civic is the relating-to-citizens word.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ic 意为「与……相关」，所以 civic 就是「与公民相关」的词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: civic duty, civic pride, civic engagement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：公民义务、市民自豪感、公民参与。

normal.en: The school subject is civics, a noun that ends in -s but takes a singular verb.
normal.cn: 学校科目叫 civics，词尾有 -s，却接单数动词。

normal.en: A civic centre is a building for the public, not a centre that belongs to a private firm.
normal.cn: 市民活动中心是为公众服务的建筑，而不是属于私营企业的中心。

abstract.en: Picture a town hall whose clock is set by the people who walk past it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座市政厅，它的钟由路过的人来校准。

abstract.en: Picture a square where every paving stone carries a name nobody reads.
abstract.cn: 想象一个广场，每块铺石上都刻着一个无人细看的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a public bench that becomes more comfortable the more it is shared.
abstract.cn: 想象一张公共长椅，越多人同坐就越舒适。

examples.en: Civic leaders met to plan the river cleanup.
examples.cn: 市政领袖开会筹划河道清理。

examples.en: The library runs civic education evenings for new residents.
examples.cn: 图书馆为新居民举办公民教育夜校。

examples.en: Civic pride showed in the freshly painted benches.
examples.cn: 市民自豪感体现在刚刷过漆的长椅上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「city（城市）+ ick（形容词尾）」——城市的、市政的；这只是一句谐音拆解，并非真实词源

root: 拉丁 civis「公民」→ civicus「公民的」→ 法语 civique → 英语 civic（十七世纪）。civis 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses stay close to one shared space: the town as a place, the council that runs it, the duties and rights of its members, the pride they feel, the engagement they show, the subject they study and the style they build.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围绕同一块共享空间：作为地方的城市、管理它的市政会、成员的义务与权利、他们感到的自豪、表现出的参与、学习的科目与建造的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone town hall on one side of a square, with notices on its steps and a clock that the passers-by keep looking up at.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场一侧的石砌市政厅，台阶上贴着通知，路过的人不时抬头看那座钟。

branches.en: The physical town and its public style are one thread: the building is the town made visible.
branches.cn: 实体城镇与它的公共风格是同一条线：建筑就是城镇的可见形态。

branches.en: The council is the town acting as an institution, so municipal government is civic in the narrowest sense.
branches.cn: 市政会就是作为机构行事的城镇，因此市政管理是最窄意义上的 civic。

branches.en: Membership runs both ways, and the same adjective names the duty to give and the right to claim.
branches.cn: 成员身份双向运行，同一个形容词既指付出的义务，也指主张的权利。

branches.en: Feeling and action support each other: pride supplies the motive, engagement supplies the deed.
branches.cn: 情感与行动相互支撑：自豪提供动机，参与提供行动。

branches.en: The idea becomes a subject when a school decides to teach it, and the adjective turns into a syllabus label.
branches.cn: 当学校决定教授这个理念时，它就变成一门科目，形容词也随之成为课程标签。

intro.en: Civic is a Latin adjective ending in -ic, and the same root also builds the person, the place, the abstract status and a school subject.
intro.cn: civic 是带 -ic 词尾的拉丁形容词，同一词根还构成指人的词、指地方的词、抽象身份与一门学校科目。

latinIntro.en: Latin civis and civicus supply the whole family; the -ic ending marks 'relating to', which is exactly the adjective's job.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 civis 与 civicus 提供整个词族；-ic 词尾标出「与……相关」，正是这个形容词的职责。

items.example: The root names the member of a town.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指城镇中的成员。

items.example: The adjective adds the relating-to ending to the root.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在词根后加上「与……相关」的词尾。

items.example: French carried the Latin adjective into modern political vocabulary.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个拉丁形容词带入现代政治词汇。

items.meaning: relating to a town or its citizens
items.meaningCN: 与城市或其公民相关的
items.example: English took the adjective in the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表关系的形容词。

items.example: The plural-looking ending names a field of study.
items.exampleCN: 这个像复数的词尾用来命名一个研究领域。

items.meaningCN: 公民的；有礼的；非军事的
items.example: A second adjective from the same root widened in a different direction.
items.exampleCN: 同根的第二个形容词朝另一个方向扩展。

items.meaning: a member of a town or state
items.example: The person-noun is the base that the adjective describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个指人的名词是形容词所描述的基础。

items.meaning: a person not in the armed forces
items.example: The word contrasts ordinary life with military service.
items.exampleCN: 这个词把平常生活与军役相对。

latinEntries.structure: civicus, civica, civicum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 公民社会；民间社会；介于家庭、国家与市场之间的自愿结社领域
definition_en: the sphere of voluntary associations, charities, unions and informal groups that lies between the family, the state and the market
core_image: 一条街上并排开着社区活动室、互助会、读书角与志愿站，几扇门都不挂政府或公司的牌子
scene: 救灾物资没有经过政府机关，而是由街角一个志愿者团体逐户分发。Aid money reached farmers through a civil society group rather than a government office.
sceneCN: 救灾物资没有经过政府机关，而是由街角一个志愿者团体逐户分发；句中这个说法指「由自愿结社与互助组织构成的公共领域」（第 1 个义项：家庭、国家与市场之外，人们自愿结成的组织与活动总体）。句意为援助款经由一个民间团体而非政府机关送到农民手中。可辨识物件：物资箱、手写名单、折叠桌、志愿者袖标。

pos.zh: 公民社会；民间社会（不可数）
（某一地的）公民社会组织总体（可数，指具体形态时用复数 civil societies）

forms.label: 相关形容词（公民的；城市的）

senses.title: The sphere of voluntary association
senses.titleCN: 自愿结社构成的公共领域
senses.definition: the area of public life in which people join associations, charities and informal groups without being ordered to by the state
senses.definitionCN: 公共生活中人们自愿结成协会、慈善组织与非正式团体的领域，不经国家指令
senses.example: Aid money reached farmers through a civil society group rather than a government office.
senses.exampleCN: 援助款经由一个民间团体而非政府机关送到农民手中。
senses.why: The phrase joins the adjective of citizenship to the noun for association, so the core image is citizens freely forming bodies of their own.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法把「公民的」形容词与「结社」名词连在一起，核心意象就是公民自由结成自己的团体。

senses.title: The organizations as a sector
senses.definition: the charities, non-governmental organizations and associations counted together as one group of institutions
senses.definitionCN: 把慈善机构、非政府组织与协会合起来算作一类机构
senses.example: The report maps civil society across twelve provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告梳理了十二个省份的公民社会组织。
senses.why: Once the sphere is recognized, its members can be counted, funded and studied, and the phrase shifts from an idea to a list of bodies.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个领域被承认，其中的成员就可以被统计、资助与研究，这个说法也就从理念变成一份机构名单。

senses.title: The third sector
senses.definition: that part of social activity that is neither governmental nor profit-seeking
senses.definitionCN: 既不属于政府、也不以营利为目的的那部分社会活动
senses.example: Foundations form the core of the third sector in that country.
senses.exampleCN: 基金会在那个国家构成第三部门的核心。
senses.why: Policy language needs a neutral name for what lies between state and market, and civil society supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 政策语言需要一个中性名称来指国家与市场之间的部分，公民社会正好提供这个名称。

senses.title: Local clubs and societies
senses.titleCN: 地方性的社团与互助会
senses.definition: the small associations of a town, such as clubs, unions, congregations and burial societies
senses.definitionCN: 城镇里的小型团体，如俱乐部、工会、教会团体与丧葬互助会
senses.example: Churches and burial societies were the first civil society in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 教会与丧葬互助会是这个镇上最早的公民社会。
senses.why: The oldest form of the sphere is face-to-face association, where membership is known by name.
senses.whyCN: 这个领域最古老的形式是面对面结社，成员彼此叫得出名字。

senses.title: Networks of trust
senses.definition: the webs of trust, reciprocity and shared norms that make collective action possible
senses.definitionCN: 使集体行动得以可能的信任、互惠与共同规范之网
senses.example: Scholars measured civil society by the density of local networks.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们用地方网络的密度来衡量公民社会。
senses.why: Association produces trust as a by-product, and researchers treat that trust as the sphere's invisible asset.
senses.whyCN: 结社会附带产生信任，研究者把这种信任视为该领域的无形资产。

senses.title: The space of public debate
senses.definition: the open arena in which issues are argued about outside direct state control
senses.definitionCN: 在国家直接控制之外讨论议题的开放场域
senses.example: A free press and open universities enlarge civil society.
senses.exampleCN: 自由的新闻界与开放的大学会扩大公民社会。
senses.why: Debate needs venues that no ministry owns, and associations provide those venues.
senses.whyCN: 讨论需要不属于任何部委的场所，而社团正好提供这样的场所。

senses.title: A check on the state
senses.definition: organized citizens able to watch, criticize and press the government
senses.definitionCN: 能够监督、批评并施压政府的组织化公民
senses.example: Civil society groups monitored the election count.
senses.exampleCN: 公民社会团体监督了选举计票。
senses.why: A body of associations can act as a watchdog, which is the political role the phrase took on in the late twentieth century.
senses.whyCN: 由社团构成的整体可以充当监督者，这正是这个说法在二十世纪后期获得的政治角色。

senses.title: Global civil society
senses.definition: transnational networks of campaigners and non-governmental organizations
senses.definitionCN: 活动团体与非政府组织构成的跨国网络
senses.example: Global civil society pushed the treaty through three summits.
senses.exampleCN: 全球公民社会在三次峰会上推动了这项条约。
senses.why: The same associational idea is lifted above the state, producing a borderless network that mirrors a borderless problem.
senses.whyCN: 同一个结社理念被抬到国家之上，产生一个无国界的网络，与无国界的问题相对应。

intro.en: Civil society joins civil, from Latin civilis 'of a citizen', to society, from Latin societas 'association'. Its meaning has reversed once: in early modern philosophy it named political society under a government, and only later the voluntary sphere outside the state.
intro.cn: civil society 把出自拉丁 civilis「公民的」的 civil 与出自拉丁 societas「结社」的 society 连在一起。它的含义曾发生过一次反转：在早期近代哲学里指受政府统治的政治社会，后来才指国家之外的自愿领域。

items.en: Civilis meant 'of a citizen, of public life', from civis 'citizen'. It described the law and conduct of members of a commonwealth rather than the private household.
items.cn: civilis 意为「公民的、公共生活的」，出自 civis「公民」。它描述的是共同体成员的法律与行为，而非私人家庭。

items.en: Societas meant 'association, fellowship, alliance', from socius 'companion, ally'. The deeper origin of socius is not established; a link to a verb meaning 'follow' is a hypothesis, not a proven derivation.
items.cn: societas 意为「结社、伙伴关系、联盟」，出自 socius「同伴、盟友」。socius 的更深来源未得到证明；与某个意为「跟随」的动词的联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: In seventeenth-century political writing, civil society named the condition of living under a government, contrasted with the state of nature. The phrase then meant more state, not less.
items.cn: 在十七世纪的政治写作中，civil society 指生活在政府之下的状态，与自然状态相对。那时这个说法意味着「更多国家」，而不是「更少国家」。

items.en: Eighteenth-century writers used the phrase for the polite, commercial order of a modern nation, again including its government and law rather than standing apart from them.
items.cn: 十八世纪作家用这个说法指现代国家那套有礼、商业化的秩序，同样包含其政府与法律，而不是与之分开。

items.en: Nineteenth-century German philosophy translated the phrase as bürgerliche Gesellschaft and placed it between the family and the state; English readers then inherited a narrower, non-state reading.
items.cn: 十九世纪德国哲学把这个说法译作 bürgerliche Gesellschaft，并把它放在家庭与国家之间；英语读者由此继承了一个更窄、非国家层面的读法。

items.en: The voluntary-association sense was revived in the late twentieth century, especially in accounts of dissident groups in authoritarian states. Source uncertain (first date): the exact point at which the modern sense became dominant is not fixed.
items.cn: 自愿结社义在二十世纪后期复兴，尤其在关于威权国家异议团体的论述中。首见年代不确定：现代义成为主流的准确时点并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words that share one element of the phrase or look almost identical; group two holds terms for neighbouring slices of public life.
note.cn: 第一组是共享短语中某一成分或外形极近的说法；第二组是描述相邻公共生活领域的术语。

entries.definition: The adjective alone means polite, non-military or belonging to ordinary law. It does not name a sector, and a civil servant is not a civil society.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词单独使用时意为「有礼的、非军事的、属于民事法律的」，并不指一个部门，公务员也不是公民社会。

entries.definition: The adjective for a town and its public buildings or duties; a civic centre may host civil society groups, but the two words are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 指城镇及其公共建筑或义务的形容词；市民活动中心可能容纳公民社会团体，但这两个词不可互换。

entries.definition: Society is the entire web of institutions and people; civil society is only the voluntary part of it.
entries.definitionCN: society 指制度与人的整体网络；civil society 只是其中自愿结社的那一部分。

entries.definition: The quality of polite conduct. It shares a root with civil but names behaviour, not organized public life.
entries.definitionCN: 指礼貌行为的品质。它与 civil 同根，却指行为，而非组织化的公共生活。

entries.definition: The sector of organizations that are neither public nor profit-making; it is the economist's name for roughly the same bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 既非公共部门也非营利部门的组织总体；这是经济学家对大致同一批机构的称呼。

entries.definition: The part of the sector made of charities and volunteers; narrower than civil society, which also includes unions and informal groups.
entries.definitionCN: 该部门中由慈善机构与志愿者构成的部分；比公民社会窄，后者还包括工会与非正式团体。

entries.definition: The space of discussion and opinion rather than the organizations themselves; it is one function of civil society, not its whole extent.
entries.definitionCN: 指讨论与舆论的空间，而非组织本身；它是公民社会的一项功能，不是全部范围。

entries.definition: The registered non-governmental organizations considered together; it is more formal and often more legal than civil society.
entries.definitionCN: 把已登记的非政府组织合起来看；它比公民社会更正式，也常更偏法律意义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real Latin roots, a real historical reversal of meaning and real policy phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的拉丁词根、一次真实的历史语义反转，以及真实的政策用语。

normal.en: Civil comes from civis 'citizen' and society from socius 'companion': citizens banding together as companions.
normal.cn: civil 出自 civis「公民」，society 出自 socius「同伴」：公民作为同伴结成团体。

normal.en: The phrase once meant the opposite: government under law, not the space outside government.
normal.cn: 这个说法一度意思相反：指受法律统治的政府状态，而非政府之外的领域。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: civil society organizations, civil society groups, global civil society.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：公民社会组织、民间团体、全球公民社会。

normal.en: The sector sits in a triangle: family on one side, state on another, market on the third.
normal.cn: 这个部门位于三角形之中：一边是家庭，一边是国家，第三边是市场。

normal.en: A trade union and a choir both count as civil society when they act as voluntary associations.
normal.cn: 工会与合唱团在作为自愿社团行事时，都算作公民社会。

abstract.en: Picture a street with four doors and no official sign above any of them.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上有四扇门，没有一扇门上方挂着官方牌子。

abstract.en: Picture a net woven from handshakes rather than from contracts.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网由握手而非合同编织而成。

abstract.en: Picture a chorus that can sing to the government without joining it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团，能对着政府歌唱却不加入政府。

examples.en: Donations to civil society groups rose after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪灾之后，对民间团体的捐款增加了。

examples.en: A strong civil society can expose corruption that courts miss.
examples.cn: 强大的公民社会能揭露法院漏掉的腐败。

examples.en: The summit invited civil society to sit beside the delegates.
examples.cn: 峰会邀请公民社会代表与正式代表同席。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「公民」加「社会」：公民自己结成的社会，就在国家与市场之间；这不是谐音，而是短语字面意思

root: 拉丁 civis「公民」→ civilis「公民的、公共生活的」→ 英语 civil；拉丁 socius「同伴」（更深来源不确定）→ societas「结社」→ 英语 society。短语 civil society 在早期近代指受政府统治的政治社会，二十世纪后期转指国家之外的自愿结社领域。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a sphere to its parts and then to its tasks: the voluntary field first, then the organizations counted as a sector, the third sector, local clubs, trust networks, the space of debate, the watchdog role and the global network.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个领域走向它的组成部分，再走向它的任务：先讲自愿领域，再讲作为部门的组织、第三部门、地方社团、信任网络、讨论空间、监督角色与全球网络。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street of open rooms run by neighbours, none of them bearing a government or company sign.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条由邻里自行打理的街，几间屋子开着门，没有一间挂政府或公司的牌子。

branches.en: The sphere is held together by talk: free associations and open argument need the same room.
branches.cn: 这个领域靠言谈维系：自由结社与公开辩论需要同一间屋子。

branches.en: Once counted, the groups become a sector, and policy gives the sector a neutral name.
branches.cn: 一旦被统计，这些团体就成为一个部门，政策再给这个部门一个中性名称。

branches.en: Small clubs teach people to trust one another, and that trust is the sphere's invisible capital.
branches.cn: 小型社团教人彼此信任，而这种信任正是该领域的无形资本。

branches.en: A dense field of associations can watch the state, which turns trust into political pressure.
branches.cn: 密集的社团网络可以监督国家，从而把信任转化为政治压力。

branches.en: The same pattern is repeated above the state, where problems and networks both cross borders.
branches.cn: 同一模式在国家之上重演，问题与网络都越过国界。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two Latin nouns turned English adjectives and nouns, and each half brings its own family of related words.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁名词转化而来的英语成分构成，每一半都带来自己的同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin civis and socius supply the two roots, with civilis and societas as the forms English borrowed; neither root has a single settled deeper origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 civis 与 socius 提供两个词根，英语借入的形式是 civilis 与 societas；两个词根的更深来源都无定论。

items.example: The first half begins with the member of a commonwealth.
items.exampleCN: 前半部分始于共同体成员。

items.structure: civilis (Latin adjective, 'of a citizen, of public life')
items.example: The adjective gave English civil and the first half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词给了英语 civil 以及短语的前半。

items.meaningCN: 有礼的；非军事的；民事的
items.example: The English adjective widened away from its political core.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语形容词从政治核心向外扩展。

items.example: The second root names the person one associates with.
items.exampleCN: 第二个词根指与自己结伴的人。

items.example: The abstract noun turns companions into an organized body.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词把同伴变成有组织的团体。

items.meaning: an association; the whole social order
items.example: English widened the noun from a club to all of social life.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个名词从社团扩展到整个社会生活。

items.example: The adjective marks what belongs to the shared order.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标出属于共享秩序的事物。

items.example: The verb keeps the original picture of joining a companion.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留了「与同伴会合」的原初图景。

items.meaning: the voluntary sphere between family, state and market
items.meaningCN: 家庭、国家与市场之间的自愿领域
items.example: The phrase is the topic word itself, read as two halves.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语本身就是主题词，可按两半读出。

latinEntries.meaning: of a citizen; of public life

definition_zh: 民主；民主制度；民主国家；民主精神；平等参与的组织方式
definition_en: government in which supreme power comes from the people, usually through free elections, or a state or organization governed in that way
core_image: 广场中央一只木制投票箱，衣着不同的人排队把折好的纸条投进去，箱子上没有任何人的名字
scene: 广场中央摆着一只木制投票箱，穿各种衣服的人排队把折好的纸条投进去。The committee was elected by open vote, a small democracy inside a large firm.
sceneCN: 广场中央摆着一只木制投票箱，穿各种衣服的人排队把折好的纸条投进去；句中这个词指「由人民掌握最高权力的政体」（第 1 个义项：最高权力属于人民、通常经由自由选举行使的制度）。句意为这个委员会由公开投票选出，是大公司内部的一个小型民主体。可辨识物件：投票箱、折好的纸条、排队的脚、看守票箱的人。

pos.zh: 民主；民主制度（不可数）
民主国家（可数）
民主精神；平等参与的做法（不可数）

forms.label: 名词（民主主义者；民主党人）

derivatives.zh: 煽动民众的（首成分相同，词根不同）

senses.title: Rule by the people
senses.titleCN: 由人民掌握权力的政体
senses.definition: a system in which supreme power belongs to the people and is exercised through elections, open debate and accountable officials
senses.definitionCN: 最高权力属于人民，并经选举、公开辩论与可问责官员来行使的制度
senses.example: The committee was elected by open vote, a small democracy inside a large firm.
senses.exampleCN: 这个委员会由公开投票选出，是大公司内部的一个小型民主体。
senses.why: Greek dēmos 'people' plus kratos 'power, rule' states the whole idea in two pieces: power that belongs to the people.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 dēmos「人民」加 kratos「权力、统治」用两块就说清了全部意思：属于人民的权力。

senses.title: A democratic country
senses.definition: a state governed by such a system, especially one that holds regular free elections
senses.definitionCN: 实行该制度、尤其定期举行自由选举的国家
senses.example: The new democracy joined the regional assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新生的民主国家加入了地区议会。
senses.why: Metonymy lets the system stand for the country that runs on it, so a state can simply be called a democracy.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让制度代指实行该制度的国家，因此一个国家可以直接被称为 democracy。

senses.title: Equal voice in decisions
senses.definition: the principle that each member has an equal say, whatever their wealth or rank
senses.definitionCN: 不论财富或地位，每位成员都有平等发言权的原则
senses.example: The co-op runs on democracy: one member, one vote.
senses.exampleCN: 这个合作社按民主原则运作：一人一票。
senses.why: The political principle travels into any group, because equal voice is the core of the idea rather than a constitutional detail.
senses.whyCN: 这一政治原则可移入任何团体，因为平等发言权是理念的核心，而非宪制细节。

senses.title: Majority rule with protected dissent
senses.titleCN: 多数决定并保护少数异议
senses.definition: the practice of deciding by majority while keeping the right to oppose and speak
senses.definitionCN: 按多数决定，同时保留反对与发言权利的做法
senses.example: Democracy means the losing side still gets to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 民主意味着落败的一方仍然可以发言。
senses.why: A vote alone could crush a minority, so the practice adds a protected opposition and the word covers both parts.
senses.whyCN: 只有投票可能压垮少数，因此这一做法加上受保护的反对派，而这个词同时涵盖两者。

senses.title: Direct democracy
senses.definition: decision-making by the citizens themselves rather than by elected representatives
senses.definitionCN: 由公民本人而非民选代表作出决定
senses.example: The town meeting is a form of direct democracy.
senses.exampleCN: 镇民大会是一种直接民主。
senses.why: The adjective direct marks the case where the people do the deciding in person, the oldest form of the idea.
senses.whyCN: direct 这个形容词标出人民亲自作决定的情形，这是该理念最古老的形式。

senses.title: Representative democracy
senses.definition: government through elected representatives who answer to the voters
senses.definitionCN: 通过向选民负责的民选代表施政
senses.example: Most large states practise representative democracy.
senses.exampleCN: 多数大国实行代议制民主。
senses.why: Scale forces delegation: millions cannot meet in one square, so the people send representatives and keep the name.
senses.whyCN: 规模迫使权力下放：数百万人无法聚在同一广场，于是人民派出代表，却保留了这个名称。

senses.title: A way of life without hierarchy
senses.titleCN: 一种削平等级的生活方式
senses.definition: a social order in which rank and privilege are reduced in everyday relations
senses.definitionCN: 在日常关系中削弱等级与特权的社会秩序
senses.example: They demanded democracy in the classroom as well as in parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 他们要求在议会民主之外，课堂上也要民主。
senses.why: The word's modern life has stretched it from government to any relation where hierarchy is flattened.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的现代生命把它从政府扩展到任何被削平等级的关系。

senses.title: The common people as a body
senses.titleCN: 作为政治体的普通民众
senses.definition: the ordinary citizens taken as a collective force, a reading common in older political writing
senses.definitionCN: 把普通公民视为一股集体力量，这一读法常见于较早的政治写作
senses.example: Ancient critics feared the rule of the many and called it democracy.
senses.exampleCN: 古代批评者畏惧多数人的统治，并把这种统治称为民主。
senses.why: In Greek usage dēmos could mean the common people themselves, so the word named a social body before it named a constitution.
senses.whyCN: 在希腊语用法里，dēmos 可指普通民众本身，因此这个词先指一个社会群体，后指一种政体。

intro.en: Democracy is a Greek compound, dēmos 'people' plus kratos 'power, rule', which entered English through French and Late Latin in the sixteenth century. It named ancient Greek constitutions before it named modern ones.
intro.cn: democracy 是希腊语复合词，dēmos「人民」加 kratos「权力、统治」，十六世纪经法语与晚期拉丁进入英语。它先指古希腊的政体，后指现代政体。

items.en: Dēmos meant 'people, common people, district'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link sometimes proposed to a root meaning 'divide, distribute' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: dēmos 意为「人民、普通民众、城区」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人提出的与「划分、分配」词根的联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Kratos meant 'strength, power, rule'. It names power as a held force rather than authority as a right, which is why the compound stresses who is strong enough to rule.
items.cn: kratos 意为「力量、权力、统治」。它把权力看作持有的力量，而非作为权利的权威，因此这个复合词强调「谁有力量统治」。

items.en: The compound is attested in fifth-century Athens. Some early uses come from critics of popular rule, so the word may have begun partly as a label used by opponents; that reading is generally accepted but not certain.
items.cn: 这个复合词在公元前五世纪的雅典已有书证。部分早期用例出自民众统治的批评者，因此这个词最初可能部分是对手的标签；这一读法一般认为是，但并非定论。

items.en: Latin had only the borrowed democratia, with no native family of its own, and Middle French democratie carried the word toward English. No Latin source forms are listed because the borrowing has no Latin root behind it.
items.cn: 拉丁语只有借入的 democratia，没有自己的本族词族；中古法语 democratie 把这个词带向英语。此处不列拉丁语源形式，因为这个借词背后没有拉丁词根。

items.en: English democracy is recorded from the sixteenth century, first in descriptions of ancient Greek city-states. For a long time it could carry a warning tone, as rule by the crowd.
items.cn: 英语 democracy 自十六世纪起有书证，最初用于描述古希腊城邦。很长一段时间里，它可能带有警告语气，指「暴民统治」。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was applied to modern states with wide suffrage, and in the twentieth century to factories, schools and families. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest use for a non-state organization is not fixed.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词用于拥有广泛选举权的现代国家；到二十世纪又用于工厂、学校与家庭。首见年代不确定：用于非国家组织的最早书证并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same Greek pieces or from a similar first element; group two holds terms for neighbouring ways of organizing power.
note.cn: 第一组是由相同希腊语构件或相似首成分构成的词；第二组是描述相邻权力组织方式的术语。

entries.definition: A supporter of democracy or a member of a democratic party. Democracy is the system, democrat is the person inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 指民主的支持者或民主政党成员。democracy 是制度，democrat 是制度中的人。

entries.definition: The adjective describing anything that belongs to or supports democracy; it cannot stand alone as the name of the system.
entries.definitionCN: 描述属于或支持民主之事的形容词，不能单独作为制度名称。

entries.definition: The process of becoming democratic. It names a change over time, while democracy names the resulting order.
entries.definitionCN: 指变得民主的过程，命名随时间发生的变化；democracy 指形成后的秩序。

entries.definition: Dēmos 'people' plus graphein 'write' is the study of populations, not of rule; the first element matches but the second does not.
entries.definitionCN: dēmos「人民」加 graphein「书写」指人口研究，而非统治研究；首成分相同，第二成分不同。

entries.definition: A state without a hereditary monarch. A republic can be democratic or not, so the words overlap but do not coincide.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有世袭君主的国家。共和国可以民主，也可以不民主，因此两词有交集但并不等同。

entries.definition: Government through elected delegates, which is one form democracy takes rather than a synonym for it.
entries.definitionCN: 通过民选代表施政，这是民主的一种形式，而非其同义词。

entries.definition: Government limited by a founding law. It protects rights but does not guarantee that rulers are elected by all.
entries.definitionCN: 受根本法律限制的政府。它保护权利，却不保证统治者由全体选出。

entries.definition: Decision by the greater number, which is one component of democracy and would be a crude substitute for it.
entries.definitionCN: 按较多数决定，这是民主的一个组成部分，若单独使用则只是粗糙替代。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real Greek pieces, a real family of English derivatives and real institutional phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的希腊语构件、真实的英语派生词族，以及真实的制度用语。

normal.en: Dēmos 'people' plus kratos 'power': democracy is literally people-power.
normal.cn: dēmos「人民」加 kratos「权力」：这个词字面上就是「人民的权力」。

normal.en: The family runs democracy, democrat, democratic, democratize, democratization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 democracy、democrat、democratic、democratize、democratization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: representative democracy, direct democracy, parliamentary democracy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：代议制民主、直接民主、议会民主。

normal.en: The opposite is autocracy, where one person holds the power that the people hold here.
normal.cn: 反义是 autocracy：那里由一个人掌握此处属于人民的权力。

normal.en: One member, one vote is the smallest working model of the idea.
normal.cn: 一人一票是这个理念最小的可用模型。

abstract.en: Picture a key that belongs to everyone in the square, so no single hand can keep it.
abstract.cn: 想象一把属于广场上每个人的钥匙，没有哪一只手能独自留住它。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that weighs opinions instead of bodies.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤，称的是意见而不是体重。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the door has no lock because the lock would need a owner.
abstract.cn: 想象一间没有门锁的屋子，因为上锁就得有个主人。

examples.en: The country held its first free election after decades of rule by decree.
examples.cn: 这个国家在数十年法令统治后举行了首次自由选举。

examples.en: Workplace democracy gave every shift a voice in scheduling.
examples.cn: 工作场所民主让每个班次在排班上都有发言权。

examples.en: Direct democracy survives in a handful of town meetings.
examples.cn: 直接民主在少数镇民大会中留存下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「demo（人民）+ cracy（统治）」——人民掌权；这是拆词联想，可辅助记忆，但并非完整词源说明

root: 希腊 dēmos「人民」（更深来源不确定）+ kratos「力量、统治」→ dēmokratia「民众统治」→ 晚期拉丁 democratia（借词）+ 中古法语 democratie → 英语 democracy（十六世纪）。该词无本族拉丁词根，故不列拉丁语源形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a constitution to a way of living: rule by the people, the state that carries it, equal voice, protected dissent, direct and representative forms, everyday equality and finally the people themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一部宪制走向一种生活方式：人民统治、承载它的国家、平等发言、受保护的异议、直接与代议两种形式、日常平等，最后回到人民本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden ballot box in the middle of a square, fed by people in different clothes, with no name written on the box.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场中央一只木制投票箱，不同衣着的人往里投纸条，箱上没有写任何人的名字。

branches.en: The rulers and the ruled are the same body, so the system and the common people share one name.
branches.cn: 统治者与被统治者是同一群体，因此制度与普通民众共用同一个名称。

branches.en: A country is called by its constitution, and a large country must lend its voice to representatives.
branches.cn: 国家以宪制得名，而大国必须把声音借给代表。

branches.en: Equal voice can be exercised in person, which is the oldest and smallest form of the practice.
branches.cn: 平等发言可以亲自行使，这是该做法最古老、最小的形式。

branches.en: The counting of hands is not enough, so protected dissent is built into the same word.
branches.cn: 只数手不够，因此受保护的异议被写进同一个词里。

branches.en: The principle escapes parliament and flattens the classroom, the workshop and the family.
branches.cn: 这一原则走出议会，削平教室、车间与家庭里的等级。

intro.en: Democracy is a Greek compound of two free-standing nouns, so the word can be read as a subject and a predicate: the people, and their power.
intro.cn: democracy 是由两个独立名词构成的希腊语复合词，因此可按「主体加谓语」来读：人民，以及他们的权力。

latinIntro.en: Latin had only the borrowed democratia and no native family, so no Latin source forms are listed; the living derivatives are English or French formations on the Greek pieces.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只有借入的 democratia，没有本族词族，因此不列拉丁语源形式；仍在使用的派生词是在希腊语构件上形成的英语或法语词。

items.example: The first piece names who holds the power.
items.exampleCN: 第一个构件指出权力属于谁。

items.example: The second piece names what is held.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件指出被掌握的是什么。

items.example: The compound names a constitution before it names a country.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词先指政体，后指国家。

items.meaning: a system of rule by the people
items.example: English borrowed the word through French and Late Latin.
items.exampleCN: 英语经法语与晚期拉丁借入这个词。

items.meaning: relating to rule by the people
items.example: The adjective describes the system rather than naming it.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述制度，而非命名制度。

items.example: The person-suffix names an individual inside the system.
items.exampleCN: 指人的后缀命名制度中的个人。

items.example: The verb names the act of extending the principle.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指扩展该原则的行动。

items.example: The combining form also builds autocracy and bureaucracy.
items.exampleCN: 这个组合形式还构成 autocracy 与 bureaucracy。

items.example: A look-alike that shares the first piece but not the second.
items.exampleCN: 一个形近词，共享首构件却不共享第二构件。

definition_zh: 民主的；民主制度的；支持民主原则的；经选举产生的；平等参与的；（美国）民主党的
definition_en: relating to or supporting democracy, or organized so that every member has an equal say
core_image: 一间开着门的议事厅，座位排成半圆，没有高台，任何人举手都能拿到话筒
scene: 议事厅里座位排成半圆，没有高台，一位年轻职员举手后拿到了话筒。Delegates demanded a democratic vote on the budget.
sceneCN: 议事厅里座位排成半圆，没有高台，一位年轻职员举手后拿到了话筒；句中这个词指「与民主制度相关的」（第 1 个义项：属于或符合人民掌权这一制度的）。句意为代表们要求就预算进行民主表决。可辨识物件：半圆座位、话筒、举起的右手、计票板。

pos.zh: 民主的；民主制度的
支持民主原则的；平等参与的
（美国）民主党的；民主党人的

senses.title: Belonging to democracy
senses.definition: connected with a system in which power comes from the people through free elections and open argument
senses.definitionCN: 与权力经自由选举与公开讨论来自人民的制度相关的
senses.example: Delegates demanded a democratic vote on the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 代表们要求就预算进行民主表决。
senses.why: The adjective adds a relating-to ending to the Greek noun for people-power, so its first job is simply to label the system.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在表示「人民权力」的希腊名词后加上表关系的词尾，因此首要职责就是标出这一制度。

senses.title: Supporting democratic principles
senses.definition: favouring equality, participation, accountability and the rule of law
senses.definitionCN: 拥护平等、参与、问责与法治
senses.example: The party claims a democratic tradition going back a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党声称自己有一百年的民主传统。
senses.why: A person or party can carry the adjective as a badge, because supporting the principle is a political identity as well as a description.
senses.whyCN: 人或政党可以把这个词当作徽章，因为支持这一原则既是一种描述，也是一种政治身份。

senses.title: Chosen by vote
senses.definition: elected rather than inherited, appointed or seized
senses.definitionCN: 经选举产生，而非继承、任命或夺取
senses.example: A democratic council replaced the appointed board.
senses.exampleCN: 一个经选举产生的市政会取代了被任命的董事会。
senses.why: Election is the mechanism that turns the principle into a procedure, so the adjective often means simply elected.
senses.whyCN: 选举是把原则变成程序的机制，因此这个形容词常只表示「经选举的」。

senses.title: Open to all without privilege
senses.titleCN: 向所有人开放、不带特权
senses.definition: available to everyone on equal terms, with no closed elite
senses.definitionCN: 人人以平等条件可用，没有封闭的精英圈
senses.example: The archive made democratic access to its scans.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆让其扫描件实现人人可及的开放获取。
senses.why: The word's modern life extends the political promise to cultural and technical access, where equality is measured by who can enter.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的现代生命把政治承诺扩展到文化与技术可及性，那里的平等以「谁能进入」来衡量。

senses.title: Decided by the members
senses.definition: settled by the votes of all members rather than by a single ruler
senses.definitionCN: 由全体成员投票决定，而非由单一统治者决定
senses.example: The club reached a democratic decision after two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部经过两小时达成了民主决定。
senses.why: Any group can borrow the procedure, and the adjective follows the procedure wherever it goes.
senses.whyCN: 任何团体都能借用这套程序，这个形容词也随之而去。

senses.title: The US Democratic Party
senses.definition: belonging to or supporting the American party of that name
senses.definitionCN: 属于或支持美国那个同名政党的
senses.example: The Democratic candidate carried the city.
senses.exampleCN: 民主党候选人在该市获胜。
senses.why: Party names capitalize the adjective, and the capital letter marks a proper name rather than the general principle.
senses.whyCN: 政党名称把这个形容词大写，大写标出的是专名，而非一般原则。

senses.title: Consistent with democratic rights
senses.definition: respecting free speech, assembly, opposition and a fair vote
senses.definitionCN: 尊重言论、集会、反对与公平投票的权利
senses.example: The law was attacked as undemocratic because it banned protests.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法律因禁止抗议而被批评为不民主。
senses.why: The negative form is the common test: a rule is judged by whether it leaves room for opposition, which is the heart of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 否定形式是最常见的检验：一条规则是否给反对留下空间，正是这个形容词的核心。

senses.title: Consultative in style
senses.definition: leading by discussion and consent rather than by command
senses.definitionCN: 靠讨论与同意而非命令来领导
senses.example: Her democratic style invited disagreement in meetings.
senses.exampleCN: 她的民主作风鼓励在会上提出不同意见。
senses.why: Leadership language borrows the word for a manner of running a room, which is the smallest scale at which the idea applies.
senses.whyCN: 领导力语言借这个词指一种主持会议的方式，这是该理念适用的最小尺度。

intro.en: Democratic comes from Greek dēmokratikos 'favouring rule by the people', through French démocratique into English in the late eighteenth century. The American party name dates from the following generation.
intro.cn: democratic 来自希腊 dēmokratikos「拥护人民统治的」，经法语 démocratique 于十八世纪后期进入英语。美国政党的名称则出自下一代人的年代。

items.en: Dēmos meant 'people, common people'. Its deeper origin is not established; any root offered for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: dēmos 意为「人民、普通民众」。其更深来源未得到证明；为它给出的任何词根都是重构形式，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Kratos meant 'strength, power, rule'. Power here is a capacity to hold and use force, not a legal permission granted from above.
items.cn: kratos 意为「力量、权力、统治」。这里的权力是持有并使用力量的能力，而非自上而下授予的法律许可。

items.en: The Greek adjective meant 'of a democracy, favouring the people'. It described a person or measure on the popular side, so the political badge sense is very old.
items.cn: 这个希腊形容词意为「民主的、拥护民众的」。它描述站在民众一边的人或措施，因此「政治徽章」这一层含义非常古老。

items.en: Eighteenth-century French political writing used démocratique for the same adjective, and English took it in that form during the age of revolutions.
items.cn: 十八世纪法语政治写作使用 démocratique 表示同一形容词，英语在革命年代以这种形式借入。

items.en: The American party took the name Democratic in the 1820s and 1830s. The capital letter in Democratic Party marks a proper name, not a stronger commitment to the principle.
items.cn: 美国那个政党在十九世纪二三十年代采用 Democratic 这一名称。Democratic Party 中的大写标出专名，并不表示对原则的承诺更强。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective was applied to access, workplaces and teaching styles. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest use for each of these extensions is not fixed.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个形容词被用于可及性、工作场所与教学风格。首见年代不确定：这些扩展各自的最早书证并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek family or with a confusingly similar shape; group two holds adjectives for neighbouring political ideals.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊词族或外形近似到易混的词；第二组是描述相邻政治理念的形容词。

entries.definition: The system itself. Democratic is only the adjective, so one says a democratic state, not a democracy state.
entries.definitionCN: 指制度本身。democratic 只是形容词，因此说「民主的国家」，不能说「民主这个制度的国家」。

entries.definition: A supporter or member; the noun names a human being, which the adjective cannot do.
entries.definitionCN: 指支持者或成员；这个名词指人，而形容词不能指人。

entries.definition: To make something democratic. The verb names the change, the adjective names the result.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事物民主化。动词指变化，形容词指结果。

entries.definition: From Greek dēmagōgos 'leader of the people', where the second piece is 'leader', not 'power'. It means appealing to crowd emotions, and is not a relative of democratic.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊 dēmagōgos「民众的领袖」，第二构件是「引导」而非「权力」。它意为煽动民众情绪，与 democratic 并非同族。

entries.definition: With a capital letter it names a member of the American party; without one it means any supporter of democracy.
entries.definitionCN: 大写时指美国民主党的成员；小写时指任何民主的支持者。

entries.definition: Believing that people should have equal rights and status; it stresses equality of condition, while democratic stresses who decides.
entries.definitionCN: 相信人们应享有平等权利与地位；它强调条件的平等，而 democratic 强调由谁决定。

entries.definition: Based on elected delegates; it names one mechanism, while democratic can also apply to direct votes and everyday consultation.
entries.definitionCN: 以民选代表为基础；它指一种机制，而 democratic 也可用于直接投票与日常协商。

entries.tag: of the people, or well liked
entries.definition: Belonging to or approved by ordinary people; the word is ambiguous because it also means well liked, which democratic does not.
entries.definitionCN: 属于或受普通民众欢迎的；此词有歧义，因为它还表示「受欢迎」，而 democratic 没有这层意思。

entries.definition: Required to explain and answer for decisions; it names one quality that democratic government is expected to have.
entries.definitionCN: 要求对决定作出解释并负责；它指民主政府应具备的一项品质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Greek adjective, a real party name and real policy phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊形容词、真实的政党名称与真实的政策用语。

normal.en: The Greek ending -ikos means 'relating to', so democratic is the relating-to-people-power word.
normal.cn: 希腊词尾 -ikos 意为「与……相关」，所以这个词就是「与人民权力相关」的词。

normal.en: The family runs democracy, democrat, democratic, democratize, democratization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 democracy、democrat、democratic、democratize、democratization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: democratic government, democratic process, democratic deficit.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：民主政府、民主程序、民主赤字。

normal.en: The negative test is common: a rule that bans opposition is called undemocratic.
normal.cn: 否定式检验很常见：禁止反对的规则会被称作不民主。

normal.en: With a capital D the word names the American party; with a small d it names a principle.
normal.cn: 大写 D 时指美国那个政党；小写 d 时指一种原则。

abstract.en: Picture a round table with no head and a microphone in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一张没有上座的圆桌，话筒放在正中央。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens wider each time someone pushes it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，每次有人推它，就开得更大一点。

abstract.en: Picture a vote that leaves a chair empty for the person who disagreed.
abstract.cn: 想象一次表决，为那个反对的人留着一把空椅子。

examples.en: The union demanded a democratic ballot before any strike.
examples.cn: 工会要求在罢工前进行民主投票。

examples.en: Democratic accountability requires officials to explain their spending.
examples.cn: 民主问责要求官员解释其支出。

examples.en: The school adopted a more democratic way of choosing its head.
examples.cn: 学校采用更民主的方式遴选校长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「demo（人民）+ cratic（统治的）」——人民掌权的；拆词可助记，但并非严格的词源说明

root: 希腊 dēmos「人民」（更深来源不确定）+ kratos「力量、统治」→ dēmokratikos「拥护人民统治的」→ 法语 démocratique → 英语 democratic（十八世纪后期）；美国政党名 Democratic 出自十九世纪二三十年代。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread outward from a form of government: the system, its supporters, elected bodies, open access, member votes, the American party, protected rights and a consultative manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一种政体向外铺开：制度本身、支持者、经选举的机构、开放获取、成员表决、美国政党、受保护的权利与协商作风。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open meeting room with seats in a half-circle, no raised platform, and a microphone anyone can reach by raising a hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间敞开的议事厅，座位排成半圆，没有高台，任何人举手都能够到话筒。

branches.en: The system is defined by what it permits: a democratic order is one that keeps room for opposition.
branches.cn: 制度的定义取决于它允许什么：民主秩序就是给反对留出空间的秩序。

branches.en: Supporting the principle shows up both as a political identity and as a way of running a meeting.
branches.cn: 对原则的支持既表现为政治身份，也表现为主持会议的方式。

branches.en: Election and member vote are one mechanism at two scales: the state and the club.
branches.cn: 选举与成员表决是同一机制的两个尺度：国家与社团。

branches.en: Access is the principle applied to culture: equality measured by who may enter the archive.
branches.cn: 可及性是原则在文化上的应用：以谁可以进入档案馆来衡量平等。

branches.en: The party name borrows the adjective and capitalizes it, turning a principle into a proper noun.
branches.cn: 政党名称借走这个形容词并大写，把原则变成专名。

intro.en: Democratic is a Greek adjective ending in -ikos, and the same two pieces also build the noun, the person, the verb and the process word.
intro.cn: democratic 是带希腊词尾 -ikos 的形容词，同两个构件还构成名词、指人的词、动词与过程名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no native Latin family behind the word; Latin carried only the borrowed democratia. The living derivatives are English or French formations on Greek pieces.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有本族拉丁词族；拉丁语只承载借入的 democratia。仍在使用的派生词都是在希腊语构件上形成的英语或法语词。

items.example: The first piece names the source of power.
items.exampleCN: 第一个构件指出权力的来源。

items.example: The second piece names what the people hold.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件指出人民所掌握之物。

items.example: The adjective adds a relating-to ending to the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在复合词后加上表关系的词尾。

items.example: English took the French form in the revolutionary era.
items.exampleCN: 英语在革命年代借入法语形式。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表关系的形容词。

items.example: The noun is the base that the adjective describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是形容词所描述的基础。

items.example: The person-suffix names an individual.
items.exampleCN: 指人的后缀命名个体。

items.example: The adverb marks how a decision is reached.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词标出决定是以何种方式作出的。

items.example: The negative prefix supplies the standard test of the word.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀提供了这个词的标准检验。

definition_zh: 民主化；国家或机构转向民主的过程；让公众平等参与；使人人可及
definition_en: the process by which a state or institution becomes democratic, or by which something is opened to everyone on equal terms
core_image: 一堵旧墙被逐段拆开，墙外的人陆续走进原本只对少数人开放的房间
scene: 旧会议厅的门锁被换掉，原本只能在门外等待的人第一次走进来坐下。The democratization of the press followed the protests, slowly and unevenly.
sceneCN: 旧会议厅的门锁被换掉，原本只能在门外等待的人第一次走进来坐下；句中这个词指「一个国家或机构转向民主的过程」（第 1 个义项：权力来源与行使方式逐步转向人民的过程）。句意为新闻界的民主化在抗议之后到来，缓慢且并不均衡。可辨识物件：拆下的旧锁、新配的钥匙、走进门的人、空出的座位。

pos.zh: 民主化（不可数）
（某一次具体的）民主化进程（可数，指不同国家的案例时用复数）

senses.title: A state turning democratic
senses.definition: the process by which a country's power comes to be chosen and checked by its people
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家的权力逐步由人民选择并受人民制约的过程
senses.example: The democratization of the press followed the protests, slowly and unevenly.
senses.exampleCN: 新闻界的民主化在抗议之后到来，缓慢且并不均衡。
senses.why: The noun adds a process ending to the verb, so it names a change over time rather than a finished condition.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在动词后加上表过程的词尾，因此指随时间发生的变化，而非已完成的状态。

senses.title: Wider participation inside an institution
senses.definition: the extension of voting and speaking rights to ordinary members of a body
senses.definitionCN: 把表决权与发言权扩展到某个团体的普通成员
senses.example: The democratization of the club began with open nominations.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部的民主化从公开提名开始。
senses.why: The same word is applied to any body with members, because the process of sharing power looks alike at every scale.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也用于任何有成员的团体，因为分享权力的过程在各个尺度上都很相似。

senses.title: Opening access to knowledge
senses.definition: the process by which books, data or learning stop being the property of a small group
senses.definitionCN: 书籍、数据或学问不再为少数人占有的过程
senses.example: Cheap printing drove the democratization of reading.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价印刷推动了阅读的民主化。
senses.why: Access is a form of power, so widening it is described with the same political word.
senses.whyCN: 获取渠道也是一种权力，因此扩大它也沿用同一个政治词汇。

senses.title: The fall of an authoritarian regime
senses.definition: the historical change by which an unelected government is replaced by elected institutions
senses.definitionCN: 未经选举的政府被民选机构取代的历史变化
