senses.example: Scholars date the democratization of the region to the late 1980s.
senses.exampleCN: 学者把这个地区的民主化定在二十世纪八十年代末。
senses.why: Political science needed a neutral term for a transition that could succeed or fail, and this noun supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 政治学需要一个中性词来描述可能成功也可能失败的转型，这个名词正好提供了它。

senses.title: Electoral reform
senses.definition: the specific changes that make elections freer, fairer and more open
senses.definitionCN: 使选举更自由、更公平、更开放的具体改革
senses.example: Electoral reform was the first step in democratization.
senses.exampleCN: 选举制度改革是民主化的第一步。
senses.why: The large process is often measured by its smallest visible step, and the ballot is that step.
senses.whyCN: 宏大的过程常以最小的可见步骤来衡量，而选票正是那个步骤。

senses.title: Social levelling
senses.definition: the slow reduction of rank and privilege in everyday relations
senses.definitionCN: 日常关系中等级与特权逐渐减少
senses.example: The reform encouraged a slow democratization of manners.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革促成了礼仪上的缓慢民主化。
senses.why: When hierarchy weakens outside politics, the word is borrowed for the social change, because the shape of the change is the same.
senses.whyCN: 当等级在政治之外减弱时，这个词就被借来描述社会变化，因为变化形态相同。

senses.title: Governance reform in an institution
senses.definition: the redistribution of seats and votes on boards, senates and committees
senses.definitionCN: 在董事会、校务会与委员会中重新分配席位与表决权
senses.example: University democratization gave students seats on the senate.
senses.exampleCN: 大学的民主化让学生在校务会获得席位。
senses.why: The institutional sense is the political sense moved indoors, where the same demand is made in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 机构义是把政治义搬进室内，同样的诉求以缩小版提出。

senses.title: A historical wave
senses.definition: one of the broad periods in which many states move toward democracy at once
senses.definitionCN: 许多国家同时走向民主的若干大时期之一
senses.example: The third wave of democratization swept several continents.
senses.exampleCN: 第三波民主化浪潮席卷了数个大陆。
senses.why: Comparisons across countries turned scattered cases into waves, and the noun became the name of a period.
senses.whyCN: 跨国比较把分散的案例整理成浪潮，这个名词于是成为一个时期的名称。

intro.en: Democratization is democratize plus the Latin process ending -ation. The verb was coined in French and English at the end of the eighteenth century, and the noun followed in the nineteenth.
intro.cn: democratization 由 democratize 加拉丁表过程的词尾 -ation 构成。动词在十八世纪末由法语与英语造出，名词随后在十九世纪出现。

items.en: The base is the Greek compound dēmos 'people' plus kratos 'power'. Neither piece has a settled deeper origin, and any root proposed for dēmos is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 基础是希腊复合词 dēmos「人民」加 kratos「权力」。两个构件都没有定论的更深来源，为 dēmos 提出的任何词根都是重构形式。

items.en: French révolutionnaire writers formed démocratiser 'to make democratic' from démocratie. The verb is a modern political coinage, not an inherited Latin word.
items.cn: 法国革命时期的作者由 démocratie 造出 démocratiser「使民主化」。这个动词是近代政治新造词，不是承袭的拉丁词。

items.en: English democratize is recorded from the end of the eighteenth century, in American political writing as well as British. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 democratize 自十八世纪末有书证，见于美国与英国的政治写作。年代为约数。

items.en: The ending -ation, from Latin -atio, names an action or its result. Added to democratize, it turns a deed into a long historical process.
items.cn: 词尾 -ation 出自拉丁 -atio，表示动作或其结果。加在 democratize 之后，它把一次行动变成漫长的历史过程。

items.en: In the mid-twentieth century the noun became a technical term for regime change, studied by comparison across countries. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest technical use is not fixed.
items.cn: 到二十世纪中期，这个名词成为研究政权更替的术语，靠跨国比较来研究。首见年代不确定：最早的技术性用例并无定论。

items.en: Late twentieth-century writing extended the noun to information, technology and culture. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest citation for the non-political sense is not recorded.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的写作把这个名词扩展到信息、技术与文化。首见年代不确定：非政治义的最早书证没有记录。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek family that differ only in ending; group two holds terms for neighbouring kinds of political change.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊词族、仅词尾不同的词；第二组是描述相邻政治变化的术语。

entries.definition: To make something democratic. The verb is the deed; the noun with -ation is the long process or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事物民主化。动词指行动，带 -ation 的名词指漫长过程或其结果。

entries.definition: The system itself. Democracy names what exists; democratization names the movement toward it.
entries.definitionCN: 指制度本身。democracy 指已存在之物，democratization 指朝它移动的过程。

entries.definition: Describing what belongs to democracy; it cannot name a process without a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描述属于民主的事物；没有名词时它不能命名过程。

entries.definition: A supporter of the system; the person is not the process, though the endings look alike.
entries.definitionCN: 指制度的支持者；虽然词尾相似，人并不是过程。

entries.definition: The study of populations, from dēmos plus graphein 'write'. The first piece matches, the second does not, so it is not a political word.
entries.definitionCN: 指人口研究，由 dēmos 加 graphein「书写」构成。首构件相同，第二构件不同，因此并非政治词汇。

entries.definition: The loosening of state controls, which may happen without any transfer of power; democratization requires the transfer.
entries.definitionCN: 放松国家控制，可能并不伴随权力转移；民主化则要求权力转移。

entries.definition: A period of change between regimes; it can move toward democracy or away from it, while democratization has a direction.
entries.definitionCN: 指政权之间的变化时期；它可能走向民主，也可能背离民主，而 democratization 有明确方向。

entries.definition: An early stage in which opposition is tolerated but not yet powerful; it may or may not become democratization.
entries.definitionCN: 反对力量被容忍但尚不强大的早期阶段；它可能发展为民主化，也可能不会。

entries.definition: The process of giving people power over their own lives; it is broader and less institutional than democratization.
entries.definitionCN: 指让人们掌握自己生活的过程；它比民主化更宽泛，也更少涉及制度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Greek base, a real French coinage and a real process ending.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语基础、真实的法语新造词与真实的表过程词尾。

normal.en: Democratize plus -ation: the verb names the deed, the ending stretches it into history.
normal.cn: 动词加 -ation：动词指行动，词尾把它拉长为历史过程。

normal.en: The family runs democracy, democrat, democratic, democratize, democratization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 democracy、democrat、democratic、democratize、democratization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: political democratization, a wave of democratization, democratization reforms.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：政治民主化、民主化浪潮、民主化改革。

normal.en: The process is often measured by its smallest step, an open ballot.
normal.cn: 这个过程常以最小的一步来衡量，也就是一张公开的选票。

normal.en: The same word covers open access: the democratization of information, of reading, of technology.
normal.cn: 同一个词也涵盖开放获取：信息、阅读与技术的民主化。

abstract.en: Picture a wall removed brick by brick until the room has no inside or outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙被一块块拆掉，直到房间再没有内外之分。

abstract.en: Picture a key copied until everyone on the street carries one.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙被复制到街上每个人都有一把。

abstract.en: Picture a door that takes years to open and never opens all the way.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门要花很多年才打开，而且从未完全敞开。

examples.en: The report traced two decades of democratization in the region.
examples.cn: 这份报告梳理了该地区二十年的民主化历程。

examples.en: Cheap cameras brought a democratization of image-making.
examples.cn: 廉价相机带来了影像制作的民主化。

examples.en: Democratization stalled after the first free election.
examples.cn: 首次自由选举之后，民主化停滞了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「民主」加「化」：由少数人掌权变成众人掌权，是一个过程；这属字面拆解，并非谐音

root: 希腊 dēmos「人民」+ kratos「权力」→ 法语 démocratiser「使民主化」（十八世纪末）→ 英语 democratize；再加拉丁 -atio／英语 -ation 构成 democratization。该词无本族拉丁词根，故不列拉丁语源形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one long change: a state turning democratic, an institution sharing power, knowledge opened, a regime replaced, elections reformed, manners levelled, boards redistributed and a whole historical wave.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项追随同一场漫长的变化：国家转向民主、机构分享权力、知识开放、政权更替、选举改革、礼仪平等、席位重分，以及整场历史浪潮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old wall taken down section by section while people who used to wait outside walk into the room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堵旧墙被逐段拆下，原本在外面等待的人走进房间。

branches.en: One country's change and a whole wave of countries are the same motion seen at two magnifications.
branches.cn: 一个国家的变化与一整波国家的变化，是同一运动在两种放大倍数下的样子。

branches.en: Participation widens from the club floor to the senate chamber, wherever seats are redistributed.
branches.cn: 参与从社团会场扩大到校务会大厅，只要席位被重新分配。

branches.en: Access is the process applied to knowledge, where the barrier is a price rather than a law.
branches.cn: 获取途径是这个过程在知识上的应用，那里的障碍是价格而非法律。

branches.en: A regime falls through institutions, and the ballot is the smallest institution that can be opened.
branches.cn: 政权通过制度更替，而选票是可以被打开的最小制度。

branches.en: Manners are the last place the change shows up, because rank survives longest in small habits.
branches.cn: 礼仪是这场变化最后显现的地方，因为等级在小习惯里存活最久。

intro.en: The word is a chain of three pieces: a Greek compound, a French verb ending and a Latin process ending, each adding a layer of meaning.
intro.cn: 这个词由三段构成：一个希腊复合词、一个法语动词词尾、一个拉丁表过程词尾，每段都加一层意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies only the process ending -atio; the root is Greek and the verb was coined in French, so no Latin root forms are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只提供表过程的词尾 -atio；词根是希腊语，动词由法语造出，因此不列拉丁语词根形式。

items.example: The first piece names who is to gain power.
items.exampleCN: 第一个构件指出应当获得权力的人。

items.example: The second piece names what is to be shared.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件指出应当被分享之物。

items.example: The compound is the distant base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是整个词族的远端基础。

items.example: French revolutionary writers coined the verb.
items.exampleCN: 法国革命时期的作者造出这个动词。

items.example: English took the verb at the end of the eighteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十八世纪末借入这个动词。

items.example: The ending turns the deed into a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把行动变成过程。

items.example: The whole word names a change over time.
items.exampleCN: 整词指随时间发生的变化。

items.example: The adjective describes the end state of the process.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述过程的终点状态。

items.example: The noun names the order that the process aims at.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指过程所指向的秩序。

definition_zh: 使民主化；使国家转向民主；让机构由成员平等参与；使人人可及
definition_en: to make a state or organization democratic, or to make something available to everyone on equal terms
core_image: 一把原本只挂在经理腰间的钥匙被复制成许多把，逐个发到每个成员手里
scene: 俱乐部年会上，成员们投票修改章程，把原本由少数人把持的提名权交给全体。The club voted to democratize its rules and let every member hold a seat.
sceneCN: 俱乐部年会上，成员们投票修改章程，把原本由少数人把持的提名权交给全体；句中这个词指「使某个组织转向由成员平等参与」（第 1 个义项：把决策权从少数人手中扩展到全体成员）。句意为俱乐部投票决定让章程民主化，使每位成员都能持有席位。可辨识物件：章程册、举手表决、钥匙串、席位牌。

pos.zh: 使民主化；使转向民主（可带宾语）
变得民主；民主化（较少用）

senses.title: Make a state democratic
senses.definition: to change a country's institutions so that power is chosen and checked by the people
senses.definitionCN: 改变一个国家的制度，使权力由人民选择并受人民制约
senses.example: The reforms aimed to democratize the country's institutions.
senses.exampleCN: 这些改革旨在使国家制度民主化。
senses.why: The verb is a French political coinage from the noun for people-power, so its first use is constitutional.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是由表示「人民权力」的名词构成的法国政治新造词，因此最初用于宪制层面。

senses.title: Share power inside an organization
senses.definition: to give ordinary members a real share in decisions rather than a symbolic vote
senses.definitionCN: 让普通成员真正参与决策，而非只给象征性投票
senses.example: The club voted to democratize its rules and let every member hold a seat.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部投票决定让章程民主化，使每位成员都能持有席位。
senses.why: The same verb moves indoors, because a club faces the same question as a state: who gets to decide.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词被搬进室内，因为社团与国家面对同样的问题：谁能决定。

senses.title: Open access to all
senses.definition: to remove the cost or gatekeeping that kept something in a few hands
senses.definitionCN: 取消把某物留在少数人手中的费用或把关机制
senses.example: Cheap printers democratized reading.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价印刷机让阅读走向大众。
senses.why: Access is treated as a kind of citizenship, so widening it is expressed as making the thing democratic.
senses.whyCN: 获取被视为一种公民资格，因此扩大获取就说成「使该物民主化」。

senses.title: Spread decision-making power
senses.definition: to distribute authority across teams or levels instead of concentrating it
senses.definitionCN: 把权力分散到各团队或各层级，而非集中
senses.example: The firm democratized budgeting by giving teams a share.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把预算权下放给各团队，使预算编制民主化。
senses.why: Decentralization is the organizational form of the same move, and the verb names the move rather than the structure.
senses.whyCN: 分权是同一动作的组织形式，而这个动词命名动作本身，而非结构。

senses.title: Reform elections
senses.definition: to make the selection of officials open, competitive and fair
senses.definitionCN: 使官员的产生公开、有竞争且公平
senses.example: The charter democratized the selection of judges.
senses.exampleCN: 宪章使法官的遴选民主化。
senses.why: Elections are the machine of democracy, so improving the machine is described with the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 选举是民主的机器，因此改进这台机器也用同一个动词。

senses.title: Open membership
senses.definition: to remove barriers of birth, wealth or fee that kept a body closed
senses.definitionCN: 取消出身、财富或费用等使团体封闭的障碍
senses.example: The guild democratized entry and dropped the fee.
senses.exampleCN: 行会开放入会并取消了费用。
senses.why: A closed body becomes a public one when entry is opened, which is the membership version of the change.
senses.whyCN: 当入会开放时，封闭团体就变成公共团体，这是该变化的成员资格版本。

senses.title: Make technology affordable
senses.definition: to lower the price of a tool until ordinary people can own and use it
senses.definitionCN: 把工具价格降到普通人可拥有与使用的程度
senses.example: Cheap solar panels democratized electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价的太阳能板让电力走向大众。
senses.why: Price is the practical gate, so lowering it is described as a political opening.
senses.whyCN: 价格是实际的门槛，因此降低价格被描述为一次政治性开放。

senses.title: Level culture and taste
senses.definition: to make cultural production and choice informal and widely available
senses.definitionCN: 使文化生产与选择变得非精英化并广泛可得
senses.example: The internet democratized taste, for better and worse.
senses.exampleCN: 互联网让品味民主化，好坏兼有。
senses.why: When the gatekeepers lose their monopoly, the word spreads from politics to culture and loses its solemn tone.
senses.whyCN: 当把关人失去垄断，这个词就从政治扩展到文化，也失去了庄重语气。

intro.en: Democratize was coined in French revolutionary writing as démocratiser and entered English at the end of the eighteenth century. It is a modern political verb formed on the Greek noun for people-power.
intro.cn: democratize 由法国革命时期的写作造出，作 démocratiser，于十八世纪末进入英语。它是在表示「人民权力」的希腊名词上构成的近代政治动词。

items.en: Dēmos meant 'people, common people'. Its deeper origin is not established, and any root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: dēmos 意为「人民、普通民众」。其更深来源未得到证明，为它给出的任何词根都是重构形式。

items.en: Kratos meant 'strength, power, rule'. The compound therefore says who is strong enough to rule, not merely who is allowed to.
items.cn: kratos 意为「力量、权力、统治」。因此这个复合词说的是「谁有力量统治」，而不只是「谁被允许统治」。

items.en: French writers formed démocratiser from démocratie in the revolutionary period. The verb is a deliberate political coinage rather than an inherited word.
items.cn: 法国作者在革命时期由 démocratie 造出 démocratiser。这个动词是刻意的政治新造词，而非承袭词。

items.en: English democratize appears at the end of the eighteenth century in political pamphlets and American newspapers. Dates are approximate.
items.cn: 英语 democratize 在十八世纪末出现在政治小册子与美国报纸上。年代为约数。

items.en: The ending -ize, from Greek -izein, means 'to make or act upon'. It turns the noun for a system into a verb of transformation.
items.cn: 词尾 -ize 出自希腊 -izein，意为「使成为、对……行事」。它把表示制度的名词变成表转变的动词。

items.en: Twentieth-century writing democratized access, technology and taste, not only governments. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest non-political use is not recorded.
items.cn: 二十世纪的写作使获取渠道、技术与品味民主化，而不只针对政府。首见年代不确定：最早的非政治用例没有记录。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek family that differ only in ending; group two holds verbs that also mean widening power or access.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊词族、仅词尾不同的词；第二组是同样表示扩大权力或获取渠道的动词。

entries.definition: The long change or its result. The verb is a single act; the noun with -ation is the history it adds up to.
entries.definitionCN: 指漫长的变化或其结果。动词指单次行动，带 -ation 的名词指这些行动累积成的历史。

entries.definition: Describing a state or body that already has the quality; the verb names the act of giving it that quality.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已具备该性质的国家或团体；动词指赋予该性质的行为。

entries.definition: The system itself. One does not democracy a club; one democratizes it and hopes democracy follows.
entries.definitionCN: 指制度本身。不能说「民主一个社团」，只能说使它民主化，并期待民主随之而来。

entries.definition: A supporter of the system. The endings look similar but one names a human being and the other an action.
entries.definitionCN: 指制度的支持者。词尾相似，但一个指人，一个指行动。

entries.definition: To relax state restrictions; power may stay exactly where it was, so it is often only the first step.
entries.definitionCN: 放松国家限制；权力可能原地不动，因此常常只是第一步。

entries.definition: A phrasal verb for making something accessible; it is broader and less political than democratize.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物可及的短语动词；比 democratize 更宽泛，也更少政治色彩。

entries.definition: To move authority from a centre to local units; the units may still be run by one person each.
entries.definitionCN: 把权力从中心移到地方单位；每个单位仍可能由一人管理。

entries.definition: To extend something to all cases or all people; it stresses coverage rather than shared decision-making.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物扩展到所有情形或所有人；它强调覆盖面，而非共同决策。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Greek base, a real French coinage and four real English forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语基础、真实的法语新造词与四个真实的英语词形。

normal.en: The ending -ize means 'make', so the verb means 'make it people-powered'.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ize 意为「使成为」，所以这个动词意为「使它由人民掌权」。

normal.en: The family runs democratize, democratization, democracy, democrat, democratic, democratically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 democratize、democratization、democracy、democrat、democratic、democratically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: democratize access, democratize decision-making, democratize the workplace.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：使获取渠道民主化、使决策民主化、使工作场所民主化。

normal.en: The word pairs a direct object with a share: you democratize a rule, a board or a fee.
normal.cn: 这个词接的直接宾语总与「份额」有关：章程、董事会或费用。

normal.en: Cheap tools do political work: printing, cameras and solar panels all get called democratizing.
normal.cn: 廉价工具也在做政治工作：印刷机、相机与太阳能板都被称为民主化的力量。

abstract.en: Picture one key cut into a hundred copies in a single afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙在一个下午被切成一百把。

abstract.en: Picture a door that stops asking for a password.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门不再要求口令。

abstract.en: Picture a table where the seats are no longer nailed to the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，座位不再被钉死在地板上。

examples.en: The new law democratized access to public records.
examples.cn: 新法律使公众获取公共记录变得民主化。

examples.en: Founders promised to democratize the platform's rules.
examples.cn: 创始人承诺让平台的规则民主化。

examples.en: Cheap sensors have democratized environmental monitoring.
examples.cn: 廉价传感器使环境监测走向大众。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「民主」加「化」的动词形：把权力从少数人手里拿出来分给大家；这属字面说明，并非谐音

root: 希腊 dēmos「人民」+ kratos「权力」→ dēmokratia／dēmokratikos → 法语 démocratiser「使民主化」（十八世纪末）→ 英语 democratize；词尾 -ize 出自希腊 -izein「使成为」。该词无本族拉丁词根，故不列拉丁语源形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one verb through every scale: a state, an organization, an archive, a budget, a ballot, a membership list, a price tag and a culture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个动词穿过各种尺度：国家、组织、档案馆、预算、选票、成员名册、价签与文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one key hanging at a manager's belt, copied many times and handed out until every member holds one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把原本挂在经理腰间的钥匙被复制许多份，逐一分发，直到每个成员都有一把。

branches.en: Constitutional change and company change are the same act: authority is taken from a centre and spread outward.
branches.cn: 宪制变革与公司变革是同一个动作：权力从中心被取出，向外分散。

branches.en: A club is a small state, and sharing its decisions is the indoor form of the same verb.
branches.cn: 社团是一个小国，分享它的决策就是同一个动词的室内形式。

branches.en: Knowledge and technology meet at a price: the gate is money, and opening it is called democratizing.
branches.cn: 知识与技术在价格处相遇：门槛是钱，打开它就被称为民主化。

branches.en: Who may stand and who may join are two doorways into the same room.
branches.cn: 谁可以参选、谁可以加入，是进入同一房间的两道门。

branches.en: When gatekeepers lose their monopoly over taste, the political word turns cultural.
branches.cn: 当把关人失去对品味的垄断，这个政治词就转向文化。

intro.en: Democratize is a three-piece verb: a Greek compound, a French verb ending and an English suffix meaning 'make'.
intro.cn: democratize 是三段式动词：一个希腊复合词、一个法语动词形式，以及一个意为「使成为」的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root stands behind the word; Latin carried the borrowed democratia and supplied only the pattern of verb endings, so no Latin source forms are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁词根；拉丁语只承载借入的 democratia 并提供动词词尾模式，因此不列拉丁语源形式。

items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把表状态的名词变成表变化的动词。

definition_zh: 共和国；共和政体；公共事务；公民共同体；公共领域
definition_en: a state whose head is elected and in which no hereditary monarch rules, or the commonwealth of its citizens
core_image: 一座没有王冠的市政厅，门楣上刻着「公共之事」，钥匙分放在几位民选官员手里
scene: 海岛上的最后一位国王退位后，议会宣布国家由选举产生的元首领导。The small island became a republic after the last king abdicated.
sceneCN: 海岛上的最后一位国王退位后，议会宣布国家由选举产生的元首领导；句中这个词指「没有世袭君主、元首经选举产生的国家」（第 1 个义项：以民选元首取代君主的政体形式）。句意为最后一位国王退位后，这个小岛成为共和国。可辨识物件：空置的王座、选举公告、议会席位、降下的王旗。

pos.zh: 共和国；共和政体（可数）
公共事务；公民共同体（不可数，较早的用法）

collocations.zh: 文人共和国；学术共同体
香蕉共和国；政局不稳的小国

forms.label: 形容词（共和国的；共和党的）

derivatives.zh: 出版；公布（词根相同，词义不同）

senses.title: A state without a monarch
senses.definition: a state whose head of state is elected or appointed for a term and not inherited
senses.definitionCN: 元首经选举或限期任命、而非继承的国家
senses.example: The small island became a republic after the last king abdicated.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一位国王退位后，这个小岛成为共和国。
senses.why: Latin res publica meant 'the public thing', and the phrase became the name of a constitution in which the state is not a family's property.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 res publica 意为「公共之事」，这个说法后来成为那种「国家不是家族私产」的政体名称。

senses.title: The commonwealth of citizens
senses.definition: the whole body of citizens and the interest they share, thought of as one thing
senses.definitionCN: 把全体公民及其共同利益视为一个整体
senses.example: Officials swore to serve the republic, not a family.
senses.exampleCN: 官员宣誓服务于共同体，而不是某个家族。
senses.why: Before it named a constitution, the phrase named a shared possession, and that collective reading survives in solemn speech.
senses.whyCN: 在命名政体之前，这个说法先指一种共同所有物，这一集合义仍留在庄重言辞中。

senses.title: The official name of a state
senses.definition: the word used in the formal title of many states, whether or not their politics are democratic
senses.definitionCN: 许多国家正式名称中使用的词，不论其政治是否民主
senses.example: The Republic of Ireland is a parliamentary state.
senses.exampleCN: 爱尔兰共和国是议会制国家。
senses.why: Names are inherited labels, and a title can outlive the constitution that first justified it.
senses.whyCN: 国名是承袭下来的标签，一个称号可以比最初为其正名的宪制活得更久。

senses.title: Rule of law in the public interest
senses.titleCN: 以法律与公共利益为准则
senses.definition: government by law for a shared good rather than by a ruler's private will
senses.definitionCN: 依法为共同利益治理，而非按统治者的私人意志
senses.example: Corruption is an offence against the republic.
senses.exampleCN: 腐败是对共同体的犯罪。
senses.why: The phrase's core is 'public thing', so any act that privatizes the public counts as an injury to it.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法的核心是「公共之事」，因此任何把公共据为私有的行为都算对它的一种伤害。

senses.title: A historical city-republic
senses.definition: a self-governing city, especially in medieval and Renaissance Italy
senses.definitionCN: 自治城市，尤指中世纪与文艺复兴时期的意大利城市
senses.example: Venice was a republic for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 威尼斯曾数百年保持共和政体。
senses.why: Small city-states show the form at its smallest, where citizens could meet in one square.
senses.whyCN: 小城邦展示了这种形式的最小尺度，公民可以聚在一个广场上。

senses.title: The republican order as a whole
senses.definition: the set of institutions and principles that keep a state non-monarchical and law-bound
senses.definitionCN: 使国家保持非君主、受法律约束的一整套制度与原则
senses.example: The constitution embodies the republic.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法体现了共和秩序。
senses.why: Metonymy lets the constitution stand for the order it establishes, so one can defend the republic in a courtroom.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让宪法代指它所建立的秩序，因此可以在法庭上捍卫共和国。

senses.title: An unstable state, ironically
senses.titleCN: 反讽用法：政局不稳的国家
senses.definition: used in phrases such as banana republic for a state whose economy and politics are controlled from outside
senses.definitionCN: 用于「香蕉共和国」一类说法，指经济与政治受外部控制的国家
senses.example: The coup turned the country into a banana republic.
senses.exampleCN: 那场政变把这个国家变成了香蕉共和国。
senses.why: The ironic use keeps the form's promise of public rule and points to its failure, which is why the mockery stings.
senses.whyCN: 反讽用法保留了这个政体「公共治理」的承诺，同时指向它的失败，因此嘲讽刺得痛。

senses.title: The shared realm of culture
senses.definition: a figurative community of readers, scholars or users who hold something in common
senses.definitionCN: 读者、学者或使用者因共同拥有某物而形成的比喻性共同体
senses.example: The park belongs to the republic of all who use it.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园属于所有使用者的共同领域。
senses.why: The old collective sense is revived in metaphors such as the republic of letters, where the shared thing is knowledge rather than law.
senses.whyCN: 古老的集合义在「文人共和国」一类比喻中复活，那里共同拥有的是知识，而非法律。

intro.en: Republic is English for Latin res publica, 'the public thing', through French république. The phrase named the shared affairs of citizens before it named a constitution.
intro.cn: republic 是拉丁 res publica「公共之事」的英语形式，经法语 république 传入。这个说法先指公民的共同事务，后指一种政体。

items.en: Res meant 'thing, matter, affair'. Its deeper origin is not established; the connection sometimes proposed to a root meaning 'wealth' is a hypothesis, not a proven derivation.
items.cn: res 意为「事物、事情、事务」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人提出的与「财富」词根的联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Publicus 'public' was formed from populus 'people'. The origin of populus is unsettled; a link to a root meaning 'fill' has been suggested but remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: publicus「公共的」由 populus「人民」构成。populus 的来源没有定论；有人提出与意为「填满」的词根有关，但仍属假说。

items.en: Res publica meant the public affair or the commonwealth, the thing that belongs to the people as a body. Cicero used it for the whole constitutional order, not only for a non-monarchical one.
items.cn: res publica 指公共事务或共同体，即作为整体的公民所共有之物。西塞罗用它指整个宪制秩序，而不只指非君主政体。

items.en: Old French borrowed the phrase as chose publique and later formed république directly from the Latin words. English took the French form, not the Latin phrase.
items.cn: 古法语先把这个短语借作 chose publique，后来直接由拉丁词构成 république。英语借的是法语形式，而非拉丁短语。

items.en: English republic is recorded from the sixteenth century, first in discussions of ancient and Italian city-states. The modern sense of a state without a monarch became standard later.
items.cn: 英语 republic 自十六世纪起有书证，最初见于对古代与意大利城邦的讨论。现代「无君主的国家」义后来才成为标准。

items.en: From the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the word was fixed to non-monarchical states, and it later appeared in official country names. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest use in a formal state title is not fixed.
items.cn: 从十七、十八世纪起，这个词固定指非君主国家，后来又出现在国家正式名称中。首见年代不确定：用于正式国名的最早书证并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the Latin phrase or look almost identical but come from another root; group two holds terms for neighbouring state forms.
note.cn: 第一组是共享拉丁短语或外形极近却出自另一词根的词；第二组是描述相邻国家形式的术语。

entries.definition: Belonging to a republic or supporting republican government; the noun names a supporter, while republic names the state.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于共和国的或支持共和政府的；名词指支持者，而 republic 指国家。

entries.definition: The political theory that prefers non-monarchical, law-bound government; it is the idea behind a republic, not the state itself.
entries.definitionCN: 偏好非君主、受法律约束的政府的政治理论；它是共和国背后的理念，而非国家本身。

entries.definition: From publicus 'of the people'; the adjective means open to all. It is one half of the Latin phrase, not the whole word.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 publicus「人民的」；这个形容词意为向所有人开放。它只是拉丁短语的一半，不是整词。

entries.definition: Re- plus publication, from Latin publicare 'to make public'. It means publishing again and has nothing to do with res publica, despite the shared letters.
entries.definitionCN: re- 加 publication，出自拉丁 publicare「使公开」。它指再次出版，与 res publica 毫无关系，尽管字母相同。

entries.definition: Rule by the people through elections; a republic may restrict the franchise, so the two ideals can diverge.
entries.definitionCN: 人民经选举统治；共和国可能限制选举权，因此两种理念可能分离。

entries.definition: A political community founded for common good; it translates the same Latin idea and is sometimes an official title.
entries.definitionCN: 为共同利益建立的政治共同体；它翻译了同一个拉丁理念，有时用作正式名称。

entries.definition: A union of states under a central government; a federation can be a republic or a monarchy.
entries.definitionCN: 各州在中央政府之下联合；联邦可以是共和国，也可以是君主国。

entries.definition: A state with a hereditary head whose powers are limited by law; it is law-bound like a republic but keeps the crown.
entries.definitionCN: 有世袭元首、其权力受法律限制的国家；它像共和国一样受法律约束，却保留王冠。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin phrase, a real French borrowing and real modern compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁短语、真实的法语借词与真实的现代复合词。

normal.en: Res publica means 'public thing': the state is the people's affair, not a family's estate.
normal.cn: res publica 意为「公共之事」：国家是人民的事务，不是家族的产业。

normal.en: The family runs republic, republican, republicanism, public and publication.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 republic、republican、republicanism、public 与 publication。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: a democratic republic, the Republic of Ireland, a banana republic.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：民主共和国、爱尔兰共和国、香蕉共和国。

normal.en: The oldest collective sense survives in the republic of letters, a community of scholars.
normal.cn: 最古老的集合义仍留在「文人共和国」这一说法里，指学者共同体。

normal.en: A republic is not automatically a democracy: the vote can be narrow even without a king.
normal.cn: 共和国不自动等于民主国家：即使没有国王，选举权也可能很窄。

abstract.en: Picture a house with no family name above the door, only the words public business.
abstract.cn: 想象一座门楣上没有家族姓氏、只写「公共事务」的房屋。

abstract.en: Picture a crown melted down and recast as a set of keys.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶王冠被熔掉，改铸成一串钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a square that belongs to everyone who walks across it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个属于每个走过它的人的广场。

examples.en: The constitution declares the country a secular republic.
examples.cn: 宪法宣布该国为世俗共和国。

examples.en: Citizens defended the republic against the general's claim to rule.
examples.cn: 公民捍卫共和国，反对将军的执政主张。

examples.en: The republic of letters ignored the border and read the same journals.
examples.cn: 文人共和国无视国界，读着同样的刊物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「公共之事」：国家是众人之事，不是一家的产业——这是短语字面义，并非谐音联想

root: 拉丁 res「事物、事务」（更深来源不确定）+ publicus「公共的」（出自 populus「人民」，其来源亦无定论）→ res publica「公共之事、共同体」→ 古法语 chose publique／république → 英语 republic（十六世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a constitution to a shared possession: a state without a crown, the citizen body, an official name, the rule of law, a city-republic, the order itself, an ironic failed state and a cultural commons.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一部宪制走向一种共同所有物：无王冠的国家、公民全体、正式国名、法治、城市共和国、秩序本身、反讽的失败国家，以及文化共有物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a town hall with no crown above the door, the words public business carved into the lintel and keys held by several elected hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座门楣上没有王冠的市政厅，刻着「公共之事」四字，钥匙分放在几只民选的手中。

branches.en: The absence of a crown and the whole law-bound order are one fact seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 没有王冠与整套受法律约束的秩序，是同一事实的两面。

branches.en: The shared possession is protected by law, and corruption is theft from that possession.
branches.cn: 共同所有物由法律保护，而腐败就是从这件共有物中盗窃。

branches.en: A country name is a label that can outlive the constitution it once described.
branches.cn: 国名是一个标签，可能比它曾描述的宪制活得更久。

branches.en: The city-republic is the form at its smallest, where citizens can meet in one square.
branches.cn: 城市共和国是这种形式的最小尺度，公民可聚于一个广场。

branches.en: The ironic failed state and the cultural commons both borrow the promise of shared public rule.
branches.cn: 反讽的失败国家与文化共有物，都借用了「公共治理」的承诺。

intro.en: Republic is a Latin phrase compressed into one English word, so its two Latin pieces still explain it: the thing and the people.
intro.cn: republic 是把一个拉丁短语压缩成一个英语词，因此它的两个拉丁构件仍能解释它：事物与人民。

latinIntro.en: Latin res and publicus form the phrase res publica; publicus comes from populus, whose deeper origin is unsettled, and res offers no established deeper root either.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 res 与 publicus 构成短语 res publica；publicus 出自 populus，其更深来源无定论，res 也没有已确立的更深词根。

items.example: The first piece names the thing that is held in common.
items.exampleCN: 第一个构件指被共同持有之物。

items.example: The root of the adjective names the owners of the public thing.
items.exampleCN: 形容词的词根指出公共之物的所有者。

items.example: The adjective turns the people into a shared possession.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把人民变成一种共同所有。

items.example: The phrase is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: French compressed the phrase into a single noun.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个短语压缩成一个名词。

items.meaning: a state without a hereditary monarch
items.example: English took the French noun in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十六世纪借入这个法语名词。

items.example: The suffix makes the adjective and the person-noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成形容词与指人的名词。

items.meaning: open to all; of the people
items.meaningCN: 向所有人开放的；人民的
items.example: The same adjective survives as an English word in its own right.
items.exampleCN: 同一个形容词也独立留在英语中。

items.example: A look-alike from the same adjective but a different noun, not a relative of republic.
items.exampleCN: 一个形近词，出自同一形容词却构成另一名词，与 republic 并非同族。

latinEntries.structure: publicus, publica, publicum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 共和国的；共和主义的；支持共和政体的；共和主义者；（美国）共和党的
definition_en: relating to a republic or to government by elected officials, or belonging to a party that takes that name
core_image: 公共建筑上挂着一面没有王冠的旗，旗下的人举着写有「法律高于个人」的牌子
scene: 游行队伍举着没有王冠的旗帜，要求用选举产生的元首取代王位。The republican movement demanded an elected head of state instead of a throne.
sceneCN: 游行队伍举着没有王冠的旗帜，要求用选举产生的元首取代王位；句中这个词指「主张以共和政体取代君主制的」（第 1 个义项：属于或支持无世袭君主的民选政体）。句意为共和运动要求以民选元首取代王位。可辨识物件：无冠旗、标语牌、空置的王座、人行道上的队列。

pos.zh: 共和国的；共和政体的
支持共和主义的；反对君主制的
共和主义者；共和政体支持者
（美国）共和党的；共和党人

senses.title: Belonging to a republic
senses.definition: relating to a state whose head is elected and no hereditary monarch rules
senses.definitionCN: 与元首经选举产生、无世袭君主的国家相关的
senses.example: The republican constitution was adopted in 1922.
senses.exampleCN: 共和宪法于 1922 年通过。
senses.why: The suffix -an turns the noun for the state into an adjective of belonging, as with many names of places and systems.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -an 把表示国家的名词变成表归属的形容词，许多地名与制度名都如此。

senses.title: Supporting republican government
senses.definition: favouring elected rule and opposing a hereditary crown
senses.definitionCN: 拥护民选统治、反对世袭王冠
senses.example: The republican movement demanded an elected head of state instead of a throne.
senses.exampleCN: 共和运动要求以民选元首取代王位。
senses.why: A supporter can carry the same word as the system he supports, which is why the adjective and the person-noun look identical.
senses.whyCN: 支持者与他所支持的制度共用同一个词，因此形容词与指人的名词形式相同。

senses.title: A supporter of republicanism
senses.definition: a person who works for a republic or writes in favour of one
senses.definitionCN: 为共和国奔走或撰文支持共和国的人
senses.example: Republicans marched for an elected president.
senses.exampleCN: 共和派游行要求民选总统。
senses.why: The person-noun is the everyday political label, used in pamphlets, parties and street movements.
senses.whyCN: 这个指人的名词是日常政治标签，见于小册子、政党与街头运动。

senses.title: The American Republican Party
senses.definition: belonging to the American party founded in the 1850s
senses.definitionCN: 属于十九世纪五十年代成立的美国政党
senses.example: The Republican nominee won the state.
senses.exampleCN: 共和党提名人赢下了该州。
senses.why: Party names capitalize the word, and the capital letter marks a proper noun rather than the general principle.
senses.whyCN: 政党名称把这个词大写，大写标出专名，而非一般原则。

senses.title: Irish republican
senses.definition: belonging to the movement that seeks a republic in Ireland and rejects the crown
senses.definitionCN: 属于争取爱尔兰共和、拒绝王冠的运动
senses.example: Irish republicans rejected the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 爱尔兰共和派拒绝了这项条约。
senses.why: A local political tradition can fix the word to one cause, so the adjective carries a history that the dictionary definition does not show.
senses.whyCN: 地方政治传统可把这个词固定在一个事业上，因此这个形容词带着词典释义看不出的历史。

senses.title: Republican virtue
senses.definition: the civic conduct that a republic is thought to need, such as service and frugality
senses.definitionCN: 被认为是共和国所需之公民品行，如服务与节制
senses.example: The school taught republican virtue: service before rank.
senses.exampleCN: 学校教授共和美德：服务先于地位。
senses.why: A free state is thought to need virtuous citizens, so the adjective attaches to conduct as well as to institutions.
senses.whyCN: 自由国家被认为需要有德行的公民，因此这个形容词也附在行为上，而不只附在制度上。

senses.title: Anti-monarchical in tone
senses.definition: hostile to a crown, whether or not a republic is proposed in detail
senses.definitionCN: 敌视王冠，不论是否提出完整的共和方案
senses.example: The pamphlet was banned for its republican tone.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子因带有共和倾向而被查禁。
senses.why: Opposition is the minimum content of the word, and a tone alone can be enough to earn the label.
senses.whyCN: 反对是这个词的最低内容，仅一种语气就足以招来这个标签。

senses.title: Neoclassical public style
senses.definition: the Roman-inspired manner of public buildings and monuments in a republic
senses.definitionCN: 共和国公共建筑与纪念物中仿罗马的风格
senses.example: The capitol was built in a republican style copied from Rome.
senses.exampleCN: 州议会大厦以仿罗马的共和风格建造。
senses.why: A republic borrows Roman monuments to look like a republic, so the adjective can describe stone as well as politics.
senses.whyCN: 共和国借罗马纪念物让自己看起来像共和国，因此这个形容词也能描述石头，而不只是政治。

intro.en: Republican comes from French républicain and the Latin phrase res publica. English recorded it in the seventeenth century, first for supporters of a non-monarchical state, and the American party took the name in the 1850s.
intro.cn: republican 来自法语 républicain 与拉丁短语 res publica。英语在十七世纪记录此词，最初指无君主国家的支持者；美国那个政党在十九世纪五十年代采用这一名称。

items.en: Res publica meant 'the public affair, the commonwealth'. The phrase supplied the noun republic, and the adjective adds a person-ending to that noun.
items.cn: res publica 意为「公共事务、共同体」。这个短语提供了名词 republic，而形容词是在该名词上加指人的词尾。

items.en: Publicus 'public' came from populus 'people'. The deeper origin of populus is unsettled, so any root proposed for it is a hypothesis rather than a proven derivation.
items.cn: publicus「公共的」出自 populus「人民」。populus 的更深来源无定论，因此为它提出的任何词根都是假说，而非已证实的派生。

items.en: French républicain named a supporter of a republic in the early modern period, and English borrowed both the adjective and the person-noun in one form.
items.cn: 法语 républicain 在近代早期指共和国的支持者，英语把形容词与指人的名词以同一个形式借入。

items.en: English republican is recorded from the seventeenth century, in the debates around the English revolution. Dates are approximate.
items.cn: 英语 republican 自十七世纪起有书证，见于英国革命前后的辩论。年代为约数。

items.en: The American party adopted the name in the 1850s, and the capital letter in Republican Party marks a proper noun rather than a stronger commitment to the old principle.
items.cn: 美国那个政党在十九世纪五十年代采用这一名称，Republican Party 中的大写标出专名，而非对旧原则的更强承诺。

items.en: The word also fixed to Irish republicanism and to neoclassical public architecture, and later became a general adjective for anti-monarchical feeling. Source uncertain (first date): the architectural use has no fixed earliest citation.
items.cn: 这个词也固定到爱尔兰共和主义与新古典公共建筑上，后来成为泛指反君主情绪的形容词。首见年代不确定：建筑用法没有确定的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin phrase or with a nearly identical shape; group two holds labels for people and movements on the same political ground.
note.cn: 第一组是出自同一拉丁短语或外形极近的词；第二组是同一政治地带中的人与运动标签。

entries.definition: The noun for the state itself; republican is the adjective or the person. One defends a republic, not a republican.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家本身的名词；republican 是形容词或指人的名词。人捍卫的是共和国，而不是「共和党人」。

entries.definition: The theory that government should be non-monarchical and law-bound; it is the belief, not the believer or the state.
entries.definitionCN: 主张政府应非君主且受法律约束的理论；它是信念，不是信徒，也不是国家。

entries.definition: Re- plus publication, from Latin publicare 'to make public'. The shared letters are accidental, and the word means publishing again.
entries.definitionCN: re- 加 publication，出自拉丁 publicare「使公开」。相同的字母只是巧合，这个词指出第二版。

entries.definition: From Latin publicanus 'tax farmer', not from res publica. It names a pub keeper in British English and is not a political label.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 publicanus「包税人」，而非 res publica。英式英语中指酒馆老板，并非政治标签。

entries.definition: A supporter of rule by the people; a republican may oppose a crown while still limiting the vote.
entries.definitionCN: 指支持人民统治的人；共和派可能反对王冠，却仍限制选举权。

entries.definition: A person opposed to monarchy; the word states only the opposition, while republican also implies a preferred alternative.
entries.definitionCN: 指反对君主制的人；这个词只说出反对，而 republican 还隐含一种替代方案。

entries.definition: A person who insists on government limited by a founding law; such a person may accept a crowned figurehead.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持政府受根本法律限制的人；这样的人可能接受一位挂名的君主。

entries.definition: A person devoted to a country; the word says nothing about whether that country has a crown or a president.
entries.definitionCN: 指忠于国家的人；这个词完全不涉及该国是君主还是总统制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin phrase, a real French borrowing and a real American party name.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁短语、真实的法语借词与真实的美国政党名称。

normal.en: Republic plus -an: the state-word gains an ending that means belonging or a person.
normal.cn: 共和国一词加 -an：这个后缀表示归属或指人。

normal.en: The family runs republic, republican, republicanism, public and publication.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 republic、republican、republicanism、public 与 publication。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: republican government, republican movement, Republican Party.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：共和政府、共和运动、共和党。

normal.en: The capital letter marks the American party; the small letter marks the principle.
normal.cn: 大写字母标出美国政党；小写字母标出原则。

normal.en: The word also names a Roman-style public architecture, because a republic borrows Rome's monuments.
normal.cn: 这个词也指仿罗马的公共建筑风格，因为共和国借用罗马的纪念物。

abstract.en: Picture a flag with a blank space where a crown used to be embroidered.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旗，原本绣王冠的位置留着一块空白。

abstract.en: Picture a throne turned around to face the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一把被转过去面朝墙壁的王座。

abstract.en: Picture a stone column that votes by standing still.
abstract.cn: 想象一根以「站着不动」来投票的石柱。

examples.en: Republican ideas spread through the coffee houses of the city.
examples.cn: 共和思想在这座城的咖啡馆里传播。

examples.en: The senator broke with the Republican leadership.
examples.cn: 这位参议员与共和党领导层决裂。

examples.en: Irish republicans remembered the rising every year.
examples.cn: 爱尔兰共和派每年纪念那次起义。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「共和国」加「人」：支持共和的人；这属构词说明，并非谐音联想

root: 拉丁 res publica「公共事务、共同体」→ 法语 républicain → 英语 republican（十七世纪）；美国政党名自十九世纪五十年代使用。publicus 出自 populus「人民」，populus 的更深来源无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a constitution to a flag: the state, its supporters, the organised person, the American party, the Irish cause, civic virtue, anti-monarchical tone and Roman-style stone.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一部宪制走向一面旗：国家、支持者、组织化的个人、美国政党、爱尔兰事业、公民美德、反君主语气与仿罗马的石材。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flag with no crown on it flying over a public building, and people beneath it holding a board that reads law above persons.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面没有王冠的旗挂在一座公共建筑上，旗下的人举着写有「法律高于个人」的牌子。

branches.en: The constitution and its stone face are one identity: a republic likes to look Roman.
branches.cn: 宪制与它的石质面孔是同一身份：共和国喜欢让自己看起来像罗马。

branches.en: Support and hostility are two temperatures of one stance: for elected rule, against a throne.
branches.cn: 支持与敌视是同一立场的两种温度：拥护民选统治，反对王座。

branches.en: The supporter and the virtue he is expected to show belong together, because a free state needs virtuous members.
branches.cn: 支持者与他应具备的美德属于一体，因为自由国家需要有德行的成员。

branches.en: The American party borrows the word and capitalizes it, turning a principle into a proper name.
branches.cn: 美国政党借走这个词并大写，把原则变成专名。

branches.en: The Irish cause fixes the word to one national struggle, giving the adjective a local history.
branches.cn: 爱尔兰事业把这个词固定到一场民族斗争上，给形容词一段地方史。

intro.en: Republican is a noun of state plus the ending -an, which marks belonging or a person, so one form serves as both adjective and person-noun.
intro.cn: republican 是表示国家的名词加词尾 -an，这个后缀标出归属或指人，因此同一个形式兼作形容词与指人的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin res publica and publicus supply the base; publicus comes from populus, whose deeper origin is unsettled, so no older Latin form is asserted.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 res publica 与 publicus 提供基础；publicus 出自 populus，而 populus 的更深来源无定论，因此不主张更早的拉丁形式。

items.example: The first piece names the shared thing.
items.exampleCN: 第一个构件指共有之物。

items.example: The adjective makes the thing belong to the people.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词使该物属于人民。

items.example: The phrase is the base of republic and republican.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语是 republic 与 republican 的基础。

items.example: The noun names the state itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指国家本身。

items.meaning: belonging to; a person connected with
items.example: The suffix makes one form do the work of adjective and person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀让一个形式兼作形容词与指人的名词。

items.example: English took the form in the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形式。

items.example: The doctrine-suffix turns the label into a belief system.
items.exampleCN: 表学说的后缀把这个标签变成一套信念。

items.example: French supplied both readings in one form.
items.exampleCN: 法语以同一个形式提供了两种读法。

items.example: A look-alike from the same adjective, not a relative of republican.
items.exampleCN: 一个同出该形容词的形近词，与 republican 并非同族。

definition_zh: 再版；重新出版；再次发表；新版印本
definition_en: the act of publishing a work again, or a work that is issued again
core_image: 同一本书的旧版与新版并排放在桌上，旧版泛黄，新版封面发亮，书脊上的书名一字未改
scene: 旧书库里，编辑把一部绝版多年的文集重新排印，换上新序后再次发行。The author agreed to the republication of her early essays in one volume.
sceneCN: 旧书库里，编辑把一部绝版多年的文集重新排印，换上新序后再次发行；句中这个词指「把已出版作品再次出版的行为」（第 1 个义项：对已有作品进行第二次或后续出版的行动）。句意为作者同意把她早期的随笔结集再版。可辨识物件：泛黄的旧版、发亮的新封面、排字盘、校样。

pos.zh: 再版；重新出版（不可数）
再次出版的版本（可数）

senses.title: The act of publishing again
senses.definition: the act of issuing a text that has already appeared in print
senses.definitionCN: 把已经印行过的文本再次发行出去的行为
senses.example: The author agreed to the republication of her early essays in one volume.
senses.exampleCN: 作者同意把她早期的随笔结集再版。
senses.why: Re- means 'again' and publication names the act of making public, so the word is literally a second making-public.
senses.whyCN: re- 意为「再次」，publication 指「使公开」的行为，因此这个词字面上就是「第二次使公开」。

senses.title: A reprint edition
senses.definition: the physical edition produced by the second or later printing
senses.definitionCN: 由第二次或后续印行所产生的实体版本
senses.example: The republication sold out within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个再版本一个月内售罄。
senses.why: The act and its product share one noun, so the word can name the edition that the act produces.
senses.whyCN: 行为与产物共用同一个名词，因此这个词也可指该行为所产生的版本。

senses.title: A reissue in a new format
senses.definition: a new issue of an old work in paperback, digital or other changed form
senses.definitionCN: 旧作以平装、数字或其他改变后的形式重新发行
senses.example: A paperback republication brought the novel to new readers.
senses.exampleCN: 平装再版把这本小说带给新的读者。
senses.why: Format changes make a reissue feel new without changing the text, and the word covers that repackaging.
senses.whyCN: 形式改变使旧作显得新，却不改文本，这个词也涵盖这种重新包装。

senses.title: Authorized re-publication under copyright
senses.titleCN: 在版权框架下获授权的再版
senses.definition: a second publication permitted by the holder of rights
senses.definitionCN: 由权利持有人许可的第二次出版
senses.example: The estate approved the republication after the rights expired.
senses.exampleCN: 权利到期后，遗产管理方批准了再版。
senses.why: Copyright turns a simple reprint into a legal event, and the word is used in contracts for exactly that event.
senses.whyCN: 版权把简单的重印变成法律事件，而这个词在合同里正指这一事件。

senses.title: Publication in a second outlet
senses.titleCN: 在另一处媒介再次发表
senses.definition: the appearance of the same piece in another journal, paper or site
senses.definitionCN: 同一篇文章在另一期刊、报纸或网站上出现
senses.example: The republication of the essay in a journal reached specialists.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章在期刊上再次发表，传到了专家手中。
senses.why: A second outlet multiplies readership without producing a new work, which is why the same word serves scholarship and journalism.
senses.whyCN: 第二个发表渠道扩大了读者，却不产生新作品，因此同一个词兼用于学术与新闻。

senses.title: Online re-publication
senses.definition: the copying of a piece onto a website or platform after its first appearance
senses.definitionCN: 一篇文章首次出现后被复制到网站或平台
senses.example: The blog's republication of the interview drew a legal warning.
senses.exampleCN: 该博客再次发布那篇访谈，招来了法律警告。
senses.why: Digital copying makes the second publication cheap and instant, so the old word acquired a new legal edge.
senses.whyCN: 数字复制使第二次发布廉价且即时，这个旧词因此获得新的法律锋芒。

senses.title: A second appearance in a periodical
senses.titleCN: 在期刊上的第二次出现
senses.definition: the later printing of a story or article in the same or another magazine
senses.definitionCN: 一篇故事或文章在同一或另一杂志上的较晚印行
senses.example: The story's republication in the magazine came twenty years later.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇小说二十年后才在该杂志再次刊出。
senses.why: Periodicals reuse their own archive, and the word marks that reuse as a dated bibliographic event.
senses.whyCN: 期刊会重复使用自己的存档，这个词把这种重复使用标为一个有年代的文献事件。

senses.title: A bibliographic record of reissue
senses.titleCN: 文献记录中的再版事项
senses.definition: the catalogued fact that a text has been issued again, with its date and publisher
senses.definitionCN: 被编目记录的「文本再次发行」这一事实，含年代与出版者
senses.example: The catalogue lists every republication of the text.
senses.exampleCN: 目录列出了该文本的每一次再版。
senses.why: Libraries need to distinguish editions, so the word becomes a countable entry in a catalogue rather than a general process.
senses.whyCN: 图书馆需要区分不同版本，因此这个词变成目录中可数的条目，而非笼统的过程。

intro.en: Republication is re- 'again' plus publication, from Latin publicare 'to make public'. It has nothing to do with republic, despite the shared letters, and it names a second issuing of a text.
intro.cn: republication 由 re-「再次」加 publication 构成，后者出自拉丁 publicare「使公开」。它与 republic 毫无关系，尽管字母相同；这个词指文本的第二次发行。

items.en: Publicare meant 'to make public, to open to all'. It was built on publicus 'of the people', so publication originally meant bringing something into the public realm.
items.cn: publicare 意为「使公开、向所有人开放」。它由 publicus「人民的」构成，因此 publication 最初指把某物带入公共领域。

items.en: Publicatio named the act of making public. Its ending -atio is the same process ending that later formed republication in English.
items.cn: publicatio 指「使公开」的行为。它的词尾 -atio 正是后来在英语中构成 republication 的那个表过程词尾。

items.en: English publication is recorded from the late Middle Ages, first for the act of making something known and later for the printing of a book.
items.cn: 英语 publication 自中世纪末期有书证，先指使某事为人所知的行为，后指书籍的印行。

items.en: The Latin prefix re- means 'again, back'. Attached to publication it marks a second or later issuing rather than a first one.
items.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 意为「再次、回」。加在 publication 上，它标出第二次或后续发行，而非首次。

items.en: English republication is recorded from the seventeenth century, when reprinted books and reused pamphlets needed a name. Source uncertain (first date): the exact earliest citation is not fixed.
items.cn: 英语 republication 自十七世纪起有书证，当时重印的书与重复使用的小册子需要一个名称。首见年代不确定：确切的最早书证并无定论。

items.en: In the late twentieth century the word extended to copying a piece onto a website. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest online citation is not recorded.
items.cn: 到二十世纪后期，这个词扩展到把文章复制到网站上。首见年代不确定：最早的网络书证没有记录。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the same Latin root or look almost identical but mean something else; group two holds terms for the various ways a work is issued again.
note.cn: 第一组是共享拉丁词根或外形极近却含义不同的词；第二组是描述作品再次发行的各种说法。

entries.definition: The general noun for making a work public. Republication is a second publication, so every republication is a publication but not the reverse.
entries.definitionCN: 指使作品公开的一般名词。republication 是第二次出版，因此每次再版都是出版，反之不成立。

entries.definition: From res publica 'the public thing', meaning a state without a monarch. The shared letters are pure coincidence of spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 res publica「公共之事」，指无君主的国家。相同的字母纯属拼写巧合。

entries.definition: A supporter of a republic or an American party member; it comes from the state-word, not from publication.
entries.definitionCN: 指共和国的支持者或美国政党成员；它出自表示国家的词，而非 publication。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to publish again. The noun adds the process ending -ation to that verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为再次出版。名词在这个动词后加上表过程的词尾 -ation。

entries.tag: a copy, not a new edition
entries.definition: A new printing of an existing text, often without changes; it is the physical copy, while republication can also mean a new edition or outlet.
entries.definitionCN: 对已有文本的新印行，往往不加改动；它指实体印本，而 republication 也可指新版本或新发表渠道。

entries.definition: To make an old item available again, often with new packaging; the word stresses availability rather than publication.
entries.definitionCN: 使旧物重新可得，常换新包装；它强调可获得性，而非出版行为。

entries.definition: An edition with changes, notes or a new introduction; a republication may be a new edition, but it can also be an unchanged reprint.
entries.definitionCN: 带有改动、注释或新序的版本；再版可能是新版，也可能是未改动的重印。

entries.definition: The reuse of a scholarly article in another venue, a term common in publishing ethics; it is one kind of republication.
entries.definitionCN: 学术文章在另一处再次使用，是出版伦理中的术语；它是再版的一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin verb, a real process ending and a real prefix meaning 'again'.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的表过程词尾，以及真实的意为「再次」的前缀。

normal.en: Re- means again, publication means making public: a second making-public.
normal.cn: re- 意为再次，publication 意为使公开：第二次使公开。

normal.en: The family runs publish, publication, publisher, republish, republication.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 publish、publication、publisher、republish、republication。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: authorize republication, republication rights, digital republication.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：授权再版、再版权、数字再版。

normal.en: The word looks like republic but is not related: one is about public affairs, the other about printing again.
normal.cn: 这个词看起来像 republic，却并无关系：一个讲公共事务，一个讲再次印行。

normal.en: A catalogue entry can count republications, which shows the word can name a single dated event.
normal.cn: 目录条目可以数出每一次再版，说明这个词能指一个有日期的单次事件。

abstract.en: Picture an old book that comes back wearing a new coat but saying the same words.
abstract.cn: 想象一本旧书换了新外套回来，说的还是同样的话。

abstract.en: Picture a letter posted twice, the second envelope newer than the first.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信被寄了两次，第二个信封比第一个新。

abstract.en: Picture a page that moves from one window to another without changing its text.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸从一个窗口移到另一个窗口，文字一字未改。

examples.en: The library ordered a republication of the 1920 atlas.
examples.cn: 图书馆订购了那本 1920 年地图集的再版本。

examples.en: Republication required the permission of the original publisher.
examples.cn: 再版需要原出版者的许可。

examples.en: Her essay found a wider audience through republication online.
examples.cn: 她的文章经网络再发布获得了更多读者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「再次」加「出版」：同一作品第二次公开印行；这属字面拆解，与 republic 无词源关系

root: 拉丁 publicus「人民的、公共的」→ publicare「使公开」→ publicatio「使公开的行为」→ 英语 publication；加拉丁前缀 re-「再次」构成 republication（十七世纪）。与 res publica／republic 无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one text through its second life: the act, the printed edition, a new format, a rights question, a second outlet, a website, a magazine archive and a catalogue entry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项追随同一文本的第二次生命：行为、印本、新形式、权利问题、第二个渠道、网站、期刊存档与目录条目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old book and a new one side by side on a desk, the old copy yellowed, the new cover bright, the title on both spines identical.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上并排放着一本旧书与一本新书，旧本泛黄，新封面发亮，两个书脊上的书名完全相同。

branches.en: The act and its catalogue entry are the same event: one is lived, the other recorded.
branches.cn: 行为与它的目录条目是同一事件：一个被经历，一个被记录。

branches.en: A reprint and a reformatted reissue differ only in the coat the text wears.
branches.cn: 重印本与换形式的再版本，差别只在文本所穿的外套。

branches.en: Copyright turns a reprint into a legal question, which is why contracts name the act.
branches.cn: 版权把重印变成法律问题，因此合同要指名这一行为。

branches.en: A second outlet and a magazine's own archive are two ways of showing the same text twice.
branches.cn: 第二个发表渠道与杂志自家存档，是让同一文本出现两次的两种方式。

branches.en: The website makes the second publication instant, cheap and legally exposed.
branches.cn: 网站使第二次发布即时、廉价，同时暴露于法律风险。

intro.en: The word is three pieces: a Latin verb of making public, a Latin process ending and a Latin prefix meaning 'again'.
intro.cn: 这个词由三段构成：一个意为「使公开」的拉丁动词、一个拉丁表过程词尾，以及一个意为「再次」的拉丁前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin publicare and publicatio supply the base; publicus goes back to populus, whose deeper origin is unsettled, and res publica is a separate phrase that produced republic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 publicare 与 publicatio 提供基础；publicus 上溯到 populus，而 populus 的更深来源无定论；res publica 是另一条短语，产生了 republic。

items.example: The adjective makes the act belong to the public realm.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词使该行为属于公共领域。

items.example: The verb names the act of opening something to all.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把某物向所有人开放的行为。

items.example: The process ending turns the act into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 表过程的词尾把行为变成名词。

items.meaning: the act of publishing; a published work
items.example: English took the noun in the late Middle Ages.
items.exampleCN: 英语在中世纪末期借入这个名词。

items.example: The prefix marks a second occurrence.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出第二次发生。

items.example: The whole word names the second life of a text.
items.exampleCN: 整词指文本的第二次生命。

items.example: The verb is the deed behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词是名词背后的行动。

items.example: The simple verb names the first act.
items.exampleCN: 这个简单动词指第一次行动。

items.example: The participle describes the text after the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词描述行动之后的文本。

definition_zh: 独裁统治；专政；独裁国家；专断控制；专政时期
definition_en: government by a ruler with absolute power, or a state or period ruled in that way
core_image: 一间没有议席的议事厅，椅子都被搬走，只剩一把高背椅和一张写满命令的桌子
scene: 议会的大门被锁上，街上贴着不许集会的告示，所有决定都由一个人签发。The dictatorship lasted twelve years before the elections returned.
sceneCN: 议会的大门被锁上，街上贴着不许集会的告示，所有决定都由一个人签发；句中这个词指「由一人掌握绝对权力、不受制约的统治」（第 1 个义项：权力集中于单一统治者且缺乏有效制衡的政体）。句意为这场独裁统治持续了十二年，选举才恢复。可辨识物件：上锁的大门、告示、签字的笔、空荡的议席。

pos.zh: 独裁统治；专政（不可数）
独裁国家；专政时期（可数）

senses.title: Absolute rule by one person
senses.titleCN: 由一人掌握绝对权力的统治
senses.definition: a form of government in which one ruler holds unchecked power and no independent body can limit it
senses.definitionCN: 一种政体：单一统治者掌握不受制约的权力，没有独立机构能限制他
senses.example: The dictatorship lasted twelve years before the elections returned.
senses.exampleCN: 这场独裁统治持续了十二年，选举才恢复。
senses.why: The word adds the state-ending -ship to dictator, so it names the condition of being ruled by an unchecked dictator.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 dictator 后加表状态的 -ship，因此指「由不受制约的独裁者统治」这一状态。

senses.title: A state so governed
senses.definition: a country whose government is of that kind
senses.definitionCN: 政府属于上述类型的国家
senses.example: The country was a dictatorship for most of the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家在那个十年的大部分时间里是独裁国家。
senses.why: Metonymy lets the system stand for the country, as with democracy, so a state can simply be called a dictatorship.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让制度代指国家，正如 democracy 一样，因此一个国家可直接被称为 dictatorship。

senses.title: A period of such rule
senses.definition: the span of years during which such a government holds power
senses.definitionCN: 这种政府掌权的若干年时间
senses.example: Life under the dictatorship was tightly controlled.
senses.exampleCN: 独裁统治下的生活受到严密控制。
senses.why: The state-ending also names a stretch of time, because the regime is experienced as a period rather than a constitution.
senses.whyCN: 这个表状态的后缀也指一段时间，因为人们经历的是时期，而非一部宪法。

senses.title: Authoritarian control in an organization
senses.definition: the running of a club, team or office by one person who tolerates no challenge
senses.definitionCN: 由一人管理社团、球队或办公室，不容任何挑战
senses.example: The coach ran the team like a dictatorship.
senses.exampleCN: 这位教练把球队管理得像一个独裁政权。
senses.why: The political word is borrowed for small groups, because unchecked personal power looks the same at any scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个政治词被借来描述小团体，因为不受制约的个人权力在任何尺度上看起来都一样。

senses.title: The Marxist class dictatorship
senses.titleCN: 马克思主义的阶级专政
senses.definition: in Marxist theory, the rule of one class in the transition toward a classless society
senses.definitionCN: 马克思主义理论中，一个阶级在向无阶级社会过渡时期的统治
senses.example: The phrase dictatorship of the proletariat named a transitional state.
senses.exampleCN: 「无产阶级专政」这一说法指一种过渡性的国家形态。
senses.why: The term uses the word for absolute rule but claims a class, not a person, holds it, which is why it needs a clarifying phrase.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语借用了「绝对统治」的词，却主张掌权者是阶级而非个人，因此需要限定语来澄清。

senses.title: Arbitrary imposition of will
senses.definition: the forcing of one person's preferences on others without discussion
senses.definitionCN: 不经讨论就把一个人的偏好强加于他人
senses.example: The committee's decisions became a dictatorship of the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会的决定变成了主席的独断。
senses.why: The word can name a manner rather than a constitution, and the manner is the constitution in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可指一种作风而非宪制，而这种作风正是宪制的缩小版。

senses.title: A regime that suppresses opposition
senses.definition: a government that jails critics, bans parties and controls the press
senses.definitionCN: 监禁批评者、取缔政党并控制新闻的政府
senses.example: The dictatorship jailed journalists and banned parties.
senses.exampleCN: 这个独裁政权监禁记者并取缔政党。
senses.why: Suppression is how unchecked power survives, so the practical marks of the regime become part of the word's everyday meaning.
senses.whyCN: 压制是不受制约的权力得以存活的方式，因此政权的实际特征也进入这个词的日常含义。

senses.title: Impersonal dominance, figuratively
senses.definition: the overwhelming influence of a force such as a market or an ideology over public decisions
senses.definitionCN: 市场或某种意识形态等力量对公共决定的压倒性影响
senses.example: Critics spoke of a dictatorship of the market over public services.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说市场对公共服务形成了专断。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the idea of unchecked power but removes the person, which makes the word useful for systems without a ruler.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留「不受制约的权力」之意，却去掉了人，因此适用于没有统治者的体系。

intro.en: Dictatorship is dictator plus the native suffix -ship. Dictator goes back to Latin dictare 'to say repeatedly, prescribe', and the Roman office was a temporary legal emergency command, very different from the modern word.
intro.cn: dictatorship 是 dictator 加本族后缀 -ship。dictator 上溯到拉丁 dictare「反复说、命令」，而古罗马的这个职位是临时的合法紧急指挥权，与现代词义差别很大。

items.en: Dicere meant 'to say, to speak'. Its older Indo-European root is reconstructed, not recorded, so any form offered for it is a reconstruction rather than an attested word.
items.cn: dicere 意为「说、讲」。它更早的印欧词根是重构的，而非有记录的，因此为它给出的任何形式都是重构形式，而非有书证词。

items.en: Dictare was a frequentative of dicere, 'to say repeatedly, to dictate, to prescribe'. The repeated saying is the seed of the modern sense of ordering others.
items.cn: dictare 是 dicere 的反复形式，意为「反复说、口述、规定」。这种反复言说正是现代「命令他人」义的种子。

items.en: The Roman dictator was an emergency magistrate appointed for a limited term with wide powers. The title is generally thought to come from the consul's act of naming him aloud, though that explanation is not certain.
items.cn: 罗马的独裁官是在紧急状态中任命、任期有限且权力广泛的官员。这个称号一般认为是因执政官当众口授其名而来，但这一解释并非定论。

items.en: Dictatura named the office and its term. The abstract ending made the post a thing that could be discussed, praised or feared.
items.cn: dictatura 指该职位及其任期。抽象词尾使这个职位成为可被讨论、赞扬或畏惧的对象。

items.en: English dictatorship is recorded from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, first for the Roman office and then for absolute rule in general. Source uncertain (first date): the exact earliest citation is not fixed.
items.cn: 英语 dictatorship 自十六、十七世纪起有书证，先指罗马官职，后泛指绝对统治。首见年代不确定：确切的最早书证并无定论。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word fixed to one-party and personal regimes, and the Marxist phrase gave it a class reading; the figurative use for markets and committees followed.
items.cn: 到十九、二十世纪，这个词固定指一党制与个人政权，马克思主义说法又给了它阶级读法；用于市场与委员会的比喻义随后出现。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin dictare family that differ in ending; group two holds terms for other forms of unchecked rule.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 dictare 词族、词尾不同的词；第二组是描述其他不受制约统治形式的术语。

entries.definition: The ruler who holds the power; dictatorship is the system or period. One can overthrow a dictator and end a dictatorship.
entries.definitionCN: 指掌握权力的统治者；dictatorship 是制度或时期。人可以推翻独裁者，并结束独裁统治。

entries.definition: Describing a person or manner as bossy and unchecked; it can apply to a single decision, not only to a state.
entries.definitionCN: 描述人或作风专断、不受制约；它可用于单个决定，而不只用于国家。

entries.definition: To say words for someone to write down, or to impose terms. The verb keeps the old speaking sense that the noun has lost.
entries.definitionCN: 指口述让人记录，或强加条件。这个动词保留了名词已失去的古老「言说」义。

entries.definition: The exercise of writing down spoken words; it shares the root but means a classroom task, not a regime.
entries.definitionCN: 把说出的话写下来的练习；它同根，却指课堂任务，而非政权。

entries.definition: Rule by one person with unrestricted power; it often implies a formal claim to sole authority, while dictatorship stresses seizure and control.
entries.definitionCN: 由一人掌握不受限制的权力；它常隐含对唯一权威的正式主张，而 dictatorship 强调夺取与控制。

entries.definition: Unjust or cruel use of power; the word judges the rule as oppressive, while dictatorship describes its structure.
entries.definitionCN: 不义或残酷地使用权力；这个词评判统治为压迫，而 dictatorship 描述其结构。

entries.definition: A system that seeks to control every part of public and private life; it is a stronger, more specific claim than dictatorship.
entries.definitionCN: 试图控制公共与私人生活每一部分的制度；它比 dictatorship 是更强、更具体的断言。

entries.definition: Absolute rule exercised at a ruler's whim; it stresses caprice, while dictatorship stresses the absence of checks.
entries.definitionCN: 按统治者心意行使的绝对统治；它强调任意性，而 dictatorship 强调缺乏制衡。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin verb, a real Roman office and a real native suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的罗马官职与真实的本族后缀。

normal.en: Dictate, dictator, dictatorship: the verb of speaking becomes the person who orders and the system he creates.
normal.cn: dictate、dictator、dictatorship：言说的动词变成发令的人，再变成他所建立的制度。

normal.en: The family runs dictate, dictation, dictator, dictatorial, dictatorship.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dictate、dictation、dictator、dictatorial、dictatorship。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: military dictatorship, overthrow a dictatorship, dictatorship of the proletariat.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：军事独裁、推翻独裁政权、无产阶级专政。

normal.en: The Roman dictator was legal and temporary, which is the opposite of the modern word's tone.
normal.cn: 罗马独裁官是合法且临时的，这恰与现代词义的语气相反。

normal.en: The word can shrink to a committee chair or grow to a whole state, because unchecked power has no fixed size.
normal.cn: 这个词可以缩小到委员会主席，也可以放大到整个国家，因为不受制约的权力没有固定尺度。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting room with every chair removed except one.
abstract.cn: 想象一间会议室，除了中间一把椅子，其余全被搬走。

abstract.en: Picture a single pen that signs every page in the building.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔签下这栋楼里的每一页文件。

abstract.en: Picture a door locked from the inside with no key on the outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇从里面锁上的门，外面没有钥匙。

examples.en: The revolution ended a dictatorship that had lasted thirty years.
examples.cn: 这场革命结束了一个持续三十年的独裁政权。

examples.en: Scholars compare dictatorship with other forms of unchecked rule.
examples.cn: 学者把独裁统治与其他不受制约的统治形式作比较。

examples.en: The board's dictatorship of the agenda silenced every objection.
examples.cn: 董事会对议程的专断压下了所有反对意见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「口述」加「人」再加「状态」：一个人说了算的状态；这属构词说明，并非谐音联想

root: 拉丁 dicere「说」（更早印欧词根为重构形式）→ dictare「反复说、口述、规定」→ dictator（罗马临时独裁官，称号来源一般认为是当众口授其名，但非定论）→ dictatura；英语 dictator 加本族后缀 -ship 构成 dictatorship。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow unchecked power from a state to a metaphor: one ruler, the country, the period, a small team, a class, a manner, a repressive regime and finally an impersonal force.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让不受制约的权力从国家走向比喻：一个统治者、国家、时期、小团队、阶级、作风、压制性政权，最后是一股非人格力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chamber with every seat removed but one high chair, and a desk covered with signed orders.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间议席全被搬走的厅堂，只剩一把高背椅，桌上堆满签过字的命令。

branches.en: The unchecked ruler and the suppressed opposition are cause and effect: power survives by silencing challenge.
branches.cn: 不受制约的统治者与被压制的反对派是因果：权力靠消音挑战而存活。

branches.en: The country and the years are one regime seen as territory and as time.
branches.cn: 国家与年代是同一政权在空间与时间上的两种呈现。

branches.en: A team is a small state, and one coach can reproduce the whole structure in a locker room.
branches.cn: 球队是一个小国，一位教练就能在更衣室里复制整套结构。

branches.en: The class version keeps absolute rule but changes the ruler from a person to a group.
branches.cn: 阶级版本保留绝对统治，却把统治者从个人换成群体。

branches.en: A manner and a market are both despotism without a face: the will is still imposed, but no one wears the crown.
branches.cn: 一种作风与一个市场都是没有面孔的专断：意志仍被强加，却无人戴冠。

intro.en: Dictatorship is a Latin person-noun plus a native state-suffix, so the word reads as the condition created by a dictator.
intro.cn: dictatorship 是拉丁指人名词加本族表状态后缀，因此这个词可读作「独裁者所造成的状态」。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicere and dictare supply the root, dictator and dictatura supply the person and the office; the state-suffix is native English and historically related to shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dicere 与 dictare 提供词根，dictator 与 dictatura 提供指人的词与职位；表状态的后缀是本族英语成分，历史上与 shape 相关。

items.example: The root names the act of speaking.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指言说的行为。

items.example: The repeated form adds authority to mere speech.
items.exampleCN: 反复形式在单纯言说之上加上了权威。

items.meaning: one who dictates; the Roman emergency magistrate
items.meaningCN: 发令者；罗马临时独裁官
items.example: The person-noun carries the office into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个指人的名词把该职位带入英语。

items.example: The abstract noun names the post and its term.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词指职位及其任期。

items.meaning: to say for writing; to impose
items.example: English kept the verb with its old speaking sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留了这个动词古老的言说义。

items.example: The native suffix makes the person into a system.
items.exampleCN: 本族后缀把个人变成一种制度。

items.meaningCN: 不受制约的独裁者统治
items.example: The whole word names the condition, not the person.
items.exampleCN: 整词指状态，而非个人。

items.example: The adjective can describe a manner as well as a regime.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词既可描述政权，也可描述作风。

items.meaning: the act of dictating; a writing exercise
items.example: The same root survives in a classroom task.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根以课堂任务的形式留存。

definition_zh: 独裁者；专政者；古罗马独裁官；专横的人；口述者
definition_en: a ruler who holds absolute power, especially one who seizes it and rules without checks
core_image: 一个站在高台上的人，台下的人排队递交请愿，台上只有一支笔和一个印章
scene: 广场广播里，一个人的声音宣布取消原定的投票，人群在台下沉默。The dictator cancelled the vote and ruled by decree for a decade.
sceneCN: 广场广播里，一个人的声音宣布取消原定的投票，人群在台下沉默；句中这个词指「掌握绝对权力、尤其以夺取方式取得政权的统治者」（第 1 个义项：不受制衡、独自掌握国家最高权力的人）。句意为这个独裁者取消投票，并以法令统治了十年。可辨识物件：广播喇叭、取消的投票牌、高台、沉默的人群。

pos.zh: 独裁者；专政者（可数）
古罗马独裁官（可数，历史用法）
专横的人；发号施令者（可数，口语）

senses.title: A ruler with absolute power
senses.titleCN: 掌握绝对权力的统治者
senses.definition: a person who holds the highest power of a state and cannot be removed by any independent body
senses.definitionCN: 掌握国家最高权力、任何独立机构都无法将其免职的人
senses.example: The dictator cancelled the vote and ruled by decree for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这个独裁者取消投票，并以法令统治了十年。
senses.why: Latin dictator named the holder of an emergency office who spoke with final authority, and English kept the person while widening the power.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dictator 指在紧急状态下以最终权威发令的官员，英语保留了这个指人的词，同时扩大了权力范围。

senses.title: One who seized power
senses.titleCN: 以夺取方式取得权力的人
senses.definition: a ruler who took office by force or by cancelling elections rather than by a lawful contest
senses.definitionCN: 靠武力或取消选举而非合法竞争取得职位的人
senses.example: The general became dictator after the coup.
senses.exampleCN: 政变之后，这位将军成了独裁者。
senses.why: The modern word is defined less by the office than by how it was obtained, so seizure is part of its everyday meaning.
senses.whyCN: 现代词义与其说由职位界定，不如说由取得方式界定，因此「夺取」成了它日常含义的一部分。

senses.title: The Roman emergency magistrate
senses.definition: in ancient Rome, a magistrate appointed for a limited term with sweeping powers in an emergency
senses.definitionCN: 古罗马在紧急状态下任命、任期有限却权力广泛的官员
senses.example: The Senate appointed a dictator to meet the invasion.
senses.exampleCN: 元老院任命了一位独裁官来应对入侵。
senses.why: The Roman office was legal and temporary, a fact that makes the modern word's tone look like a reversal.
senses.whyCN: 罗马的职位合法且临时，这一事实使现代词义的语气看起来像一次反转。

senses.title: A domineering person in a group
senses.definition: a member of a team, office or family who insists on deciding everything
senses.definitionCN: 在团队、办公室或家庭里坚持决定一切的人
senses.example: The office manager acted like a dictator.
senses.exampleCN: 这位办公室主管行事像个独裁者。
senses.why: Unchecked personal power looks the same at any scale, so the political person-word is borrowed for small tyrants.
senses.whyCN: 不受制约的个人权力在任何尺度上看起来都一样，因此这个政治指人词被借来描述小范围的专横者。

senses.title: Leader of an authoritarian state or party
senses.titleCN: 威权国家或政党的领袖
senses.definition: the head of a party or state who controls the police, the press and the courts
senses.definitionCN: 控制警察、新闻与法院的政党或国家领袖
senses.example: The party's dictator controlled the police.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党的独裁者控制着警察。
senses.why: When a party rather than a person holds power, the person at the top still carries the old title.
senses.whyCN: 当掌权者是政党而非个人时，最高处的那个人仍沿用旧称号。

senses.title: One who dictates text
senses.definition: in older usage, a person who reads words aloud for others to write down
senses.definitionCN: 较早的用法中指朗读词句、让旁人记录的人
senses.example: In the old schoolroom, the dictator read while pupils wrote.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧式教室里，口述者朗读，学生记录。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the plain one: a person who dictates words. The political sense grew out of the authority of the speaking voice.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是朴素的那个：口述词句的人。政治义从言说声音的权威中生长出来。

senses.title: The power behind a government
senses.titleCN: 政府背后的实际掌权者
senses.definition: a person who holds real power while a figurehead occupies the official post
senses.definitionCN: 名义职位由傀儡占据、实际权力归其所有之人
senses.example: The elected president was a figurehead; the real dictator sat in the shadows.
senses.exampleCN: 当选总统只是名义元首；真正的独裁者坐在幕后。
senses.why: Power without a title is still dictatorship, so the word follows the control rather than the office.
senses.whyCN: 没有头衔的权力仍是独裁，因此这个词跟随控制权，而非职位。

senses.title: A leader who dictates terms to others
senses.titleCN: 向他人强加条件的领导者
senses.definition: a leader who imposes conditions on other states or groups without negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 不经协商就向他国或他群体强加条件的领导者
senses.example: The dictator imposed terms on his neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 这位独裁者向邻国强加条件。
senses.why: The verb 'to dictate' survives inside the person-word, and imposing terms is the verb's plainest modern use.
senses.whyCN: 「口述、规定」的动词义仍活在这个指人词内部，而强加条件正是该动词最朴素的现代用法。

intro.en: Dictator is Latin for the holder of an emergency office, from dictare 'to say repeatedly, prescribe'. English took the word in the sixteenth century for the Roman magistrate, and the modern sense of an absolute ruler hardened in the nineteenth and twentieth.
intro.cn: dictator 是拉丁语中紧急状态官职的称呼，出自 dictare「反复说、规定」。英语在十六世纪借入此词指罗马官员，而「绝对统治者」的现代义在十九、二十世纪固定下来。

items.en: Dicere meant 'to say, to speak'. Its older Indo-European root is reconstructed rather than recorded, so any form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: dicere 意为「说、讲」。它更早的印欧词根是重构的，而非有记录的，因此为它提出的任何形式都是重构形式。

items.en: Dictare, a frequentative of dicere, meant 'to say repeatedly, to dictate, to prescribe'. Repetition turned speech into an order.
items.cn: dictare 是 dicere 的反复形式，意为「反复说、口述、规定」。反复使言说变成命令。

items.en: The Roman dictator was appointed in emergencies for a fixed short term and held sweeping but temporary powers. The title is generally thought to refer to the consul's naming him aloud, though that explanation is not certain.
items.cn: 罗马独裁官在紧急状态下被任命，任期固定且很短，权力广泛但属临时。这个称号一般认为是因执政官当众口述其名而来，但这一解释并非定论。

items.en: English dictator first named the Roman magistrate and then any absolute ruler. Dates are approximate, and the shift between the two senses was gradual.
items.cn: 英语 dictator 先指罗马官员，后指任何绝对统治者。年代为约数，两种词义之间的转变是渐进的。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word fixed to rulers who seize or hold power without checks, especially military leaders and party chiefs.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词固定指夺取或掌握权力且不受制衡的统治者，尤其指军事领袖与政党首脑。

items.en: The twentieth century applied the word to bosses, coaches and parents, and to powers behind elected governments. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest figurative citation is not fixed.
items.cn: 二十世纪把这个词用于上司、教练与家长，也用于民选政府背后的势力。首见年代不确定：最早的比喻书证并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin dictare family that differ only in ending; group two holds names for other kinds of unchecked ruler.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 dictare 词族、仅词尾不同的词；第二组是其他不受制约统治者的称呼。

entries.definition: The regime or period, not the person. One overthrows a dictator and ends a dictatorship.
entries.definitionCN: 指政权或时期，而非个人。人推翻独裁者，结束独裁统治。

entries.definition: Describing a ruler or manner as unchecked and bossy; it can modify a decision as well as a person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述统治者或作风不受制约、专横；它可修饰决定，也可修饰人。

entries.definition: To say words for writing, or to impose terms. The verb preserves the speaking sense that the noun has almost lost.
entries.definitionCN: 指口述让人记录，或强加条件。动词保留了名词几乎已失去的言说义。

entries.definition: The act of writing down spoken words, or the classroom task based on it; it shares the root but names no ruler.
entries.definitionCN: 指把口述内容写下来的行为，或据此设置的课堂练习；它同根，却不指任何统治者。

entries.definition: From Greek dēmagōgos 'leader of the people', built on 'lead', not 'say'. A demagogue stirs a crowd but need not hold absolute power.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊 dēmagōgos「民众的领袖」，基础是「引导」而非「说」。煽动者搅动人群，却未必掌握绝对权力。

entries.definition: A ruler who uses power unjustly and cruelly; the word judges the rule, while dictator describes how power is held.
entries.definitionCN: 不义而残酷地行使权力的统治者；这个词评判统治，而 dictator 描述权力如何被掌握。

entries.definition: A ruler who holds authority alone, often by inherited right; a dictator typically seizes power instead.
entries.definitionCN: 独自掌握权威的统治者，常凭继承权；独裁者则通常靠夺取权力。

entries.definition: A ruler whose word is law and whose choices follow his mood; the word stresses arbitrariness.
entries.definitionCN: 一句话就是法律、选择随心情而定的统治者；这个词强调任意性。

entries.definition: An informal term for a leader who rules by force and personality; it describes the style rather than the constitution.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中指靠武力与个人魅力统治的领袖；它描述风格，而非宪制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin verb, a real Roman office and a real family of English forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的罗马官职与真实的英语词族。

normal.en: Dictate, dictator, dictatorship: speaking with authority becomes a person, then a system.
normal.cn: dictate、dictator、dictatorship：带权威的言说变成一个人，再变成一套制度。

normal.en: The family runs dictate, dictation, dictator, dictatorial, dictatorship.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dictate、dictation、dictator、dictatorial、dictatorship。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: a military dictator, overthrow the dictator, a puppet dictator.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：军事独裁者、推翻独裁者、傀儡独裁者。

normal.en: The Roman dictator was legal and temporary, unlike the modern figure.
normal.cn: 罗马独裁官合法且临时，与现代人物不同。

normal.en: The word can name a general, a party chief, a boss or a coach, because unchecked power has no fixed size.
normal.cn: 这个词可指将军、政党首脑、上司或教练，因为不受制约的权力没有固定尺度。

abstract.en: Picture one hand holding both a pen and a seal.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手同时握着笔与印章。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone that no one else is allowed to touch.
abstract.cn: 想象一支不许别人碰的话筒。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow standing behind an empty official chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一道影子站在一把空着的正式椅子后面。

examples.en: The dictator banned every party but his own.
examples.cn: 这位独裁者取缔了除自己政党之外的所有政党。
