examples.en: Ancient writers described the dictator's six-month term.
examples.cn: 古代作家记述了独裁官六个月的任期。

examples.en: The team's captain behaved like a dictator on the field.
examples.cn: 这支球队的队长在球场上行事像个独裁者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「口述」加「人」：一个人说了算；这属构词说明，并非谐音联想

root: 拉丁 dicere「说」（更早印欧词根为重构形式）→ dictare「反复说、口述、规定」→ dictator（罗马临时独裁官，称号来源一般认为是当众口述其名，但非定论）→ 英语 dictator（十六世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one figure from a Roman office to a shadow behind a chair: the absolute ruler, the man who seized power, the ancient magistrate, the office bully, the party chief, the reader of texts, the power behind a figurehead and the leader who dictates terms.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个人物从罗马官职走到椅后的影子：绝对统治者、夺权者、古代官员、办公室里的专横者、政党首脑、朗读文本者、傀儡背后的实权者，以及强加条件的领袖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure on a raised platform holding a pen and a seal while a queue of petitioners waits below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个站在高台上的人手里握着笔与印章，台下排着递交请愿的人。

branches.en: Absolute power and the way it was taken are one story: the modern word begins with the seizure.
branches.cn: 绝对权力与取得方式是一个故事：现代词义从夺取开始。

branches.en: The Roman office and the classroom reader share the oldest layer, where the title meant the speaking authority.
branches.cn: 罗马官职与课堂朗读者共享最古老的一层，那里的称号指言说的权威。

branches.en: A boss reproduces the whole structure in one room, because unchecked power needs no constitution.
branches.cn: 一个上司就能在一间屋子里复制整套结构，因为不受制约的权力不需要宪法。

branches.en: The party chief and the shadow behind the chair are the same power with and without a title.
branches.cn: 政党首脑与椅后的影子，是同一权力有头衔与无头衔的两种样子。

branches.en: Dictating terms abroad is the old verb of speech turned into foreign policy.
branches.cn: 对外强加条件，是把古老的言说动词变成外交政策。

intro.en: Dictator is a Latin person-noun built on the verb for repeated speech, and the same family supplies the system, the adjective and the classroom task.
intro.cn: dictator 是建立在「反复言说」动词上的拉丁指人名词，同一词族还提供制度名、形容词与课堂任务名。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicere and dictare supply the root, and dictator supplies the person; the deeper Indo-European root of dicere is reconstructed rather than attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dicere 与 dictare 提供词根，dictator 提供指人的词；dicere 更早的印欧词根是重构的，而非有书证的。

items.example: The root names plain speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指朴素的言说。

items.example: Repetition gives the speaker authority.
items.exampleCN: 反复言说赋予说话者权威。

items.meaning: one who dictates; the Roman magistrate
items.example: The person-noun carries both the title and the office.
items.exampleCN: 这个指人的名词同时承载称号与职位。

items.example: The abstract noun names the post itself.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词指职位本身。

items.example: The agent suffix turns the verb into a person.
items.exampleCN: 施事后缀把动词变成指人的词。

items.meaning: to say for writing; to impose
items.example: English kept the verb beside the borrowed person-noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语在借入指人名词之外保留了动词。

items.example: The native suffix turns the person into a system.
items.exampleCN: 本族后缀把个人变成制度。

items.example: The adjective describes the manner as well as the office.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词既描述作风，也描述职位。

items.meaning: the act of dictating; a writing exercise
items.example: The old speaking sense survives in a school task.
items.exampleCN: 古老的言说义以学校任务的形式留存。

definition_zh: 威权的；专制的；要求服从的；威权主义者；家长式的
definition_en: demanding obedience and allowing little freedom, or relating to a system that concentrates power in an authority
core_image: 办公桌后坐着一位上司，桌上立着一块牌写着「照我说的做」，门外的人排队等候批准
scene: 新经理上任后，所有决定都要经他一人签字，员工连改一行文案也要等批准。The new manager ran an authoritarian office where no one dared to disagree.
sceneCN: 新经理上任后，所有决定都要经他一人签字，员工连改一行文案也要等批准；句中这个词指「要求服从、几乎不容自由的」（第 1 个义项：以权威为中心、限制异议与自主的制度或作风）。句意为新经理把一个办公室管成威权式的，没人敢表示不同意见。可辨识物件：签字笔、审批单、门口排队的人、写有命令的牌子。

pos.zh: 威权的；专制的；要求服从的
家长式的；管得过严的（口语）
威权主义者；主张集中权力的人

senses.title: Demanding obedience
senses.definition: expecting people to comply without question and treating disagreement as a problem
senses.definitionCN: 要求人们无条件服从，并把异议视为问题
senses.example: The new manager ran an authoritarian office where no one dared to disagree.
senses.exampleCN: 新经理把一个办公室管成威权式的，没人敢表示不同意见。
senses.why: The suffix -arian forms an adjective of adherence, so the word describes a way of holding authority rather than an office.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -arian 构成表示信奉的形容词，因此这个词描述握有权威的方式，而非某个职位。

senses.title: Relating to authoritarian government
senses.definition: belonging to a system in which power is concentrated and elections, if held, are not competitive
senses.definitionCN: 属于权力集中、即使有选举也缺乏竞争的体制
senses.example: The regime was authoritarian but kept elections for show.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政权是威权式的，却保留选举作为门面。
senses.why: Political science needed a word for systems that are neither democratic nor fully totalitarian, and this adjective filled the gap.
senses.whyCN: 政治学需要一个词来描述既非民主、也非完全极权的体制，这个形容词填补了空缺。

senses.title: A person who favours such rule
senses.definition: someone who believes order requires concentrated, unchallenged authority
senses.definitionCN: 认为秩序需要集中而不容挑战的权威的人
senses.example: Authoritarians distrust open debate.
senses.exampleCN: 威权主义者不信任公开辩论。
senses.why: One form serves as adjective and person-noun, so the believer and the belief look identical.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形式兼作形容词与指人的名词，因此信徒与信条看起来一样。

senses.title: A parenting style
senses.definition: raising children with strict rules and little room for discussion or autonomy
senses.definitionCN: 以严格规则养育孩子，很少给讨论或自主空间
senses.example: Authoritarian parents set rules without discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 专制型父母立规矩而不讨论。
senses.why: The political word is borrowed for the family, the smallest place where unchecked authority is exercised.
senses.whyCN: 这个政治词被借来描述家庭，也就是行使不受制约权威的最小场所。

senses.title: A management style
senses.definition: running a workplace by centralised approval and one-way instruction
senses.definitionCN: 靠集中审批与单向指令运行工作场所
senses.example: An authoritarian boss centralises every approval.
senses.exampleCN: 威权式上司把每一项批准都集中到自己手里。
senses.why: Workplaces reproduce the state in miniature, so the same adjective describes a chain of approvals.
senses.whyCN: 工作场所是国家的缩小复制，因此同一个形容词可描述审批链。

senses.title: A personality trait
senses.definition: a disposition that prefers rigid order, hierarchy and submission to authority
senses.definitionCN: 偏好僵化的秩序、等级与服从权威的性情
senses.example: His authoritarian streak showed in small rules.
senses.exampleCN: 他的威权倾向体现在一条条小规矩里。
senses.why: Twentieth-century psychology turned a political adjective into a measurable trait, which is why questionnaires use the word.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪心理学把这个政治形容词变成可测量的特质，因此问卷会用到这个词。

senses.title: An institutional culture
senses.definition: a habit inside an organization that punishes criticism and rewards deference
senses.definitionCN: 机构内部惩罚批评、奖励顺从的习惯
senses.example: The university's authoritarian culture discouraged criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学的威权文化压制了批评。
senses.why: Culture is authority without a visible ruler, so the word can describe an atmosphere rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 文化是没有可见统治者的权威，因此这个词可描述氛围，而非某个人。

senses.title: Order valued above liberty
senses.definition: characteristic of an ideology that treats stability and obedience as higher goods than freedom
senses.definitionCN: 把稳定与服从视为高于自由的价值的意识形态特征
senses.example: The party's authoritarian ideology valued order over liberty.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党的威权意识形态把秩序看得高于自由。
senses.why: The adjective also marks a value ranking, which is the ideological core behind the institutional forms.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也标出一种价值排序，而那正是制度形式背后的意识形态核心。

intro.en: Authoritarian is authority plus the suffix -arian, modelled on French autoritaire. English used it from the nineteenth century for systems that concentrate power, and the twentieth century extended it to personalities and management.
intro.cn: authoritarian 是 authority 加后缀 -arian，仿法语 autoritaire 构成。英语从十九世纪起用它指集中权力的体制，二十世纪又扩展到人格与管理。

items.en: Augere meant 'to increase, to grow'. Its Indo-European source is reconstructed, so the older root is a reconstruction rather than an attested form.
items.cn: augere 意为「增加、生长」。它的印欧来源是重构的，因此更早的词根是重构形式，而非有书证的形式。

items.en: Auctor meant 'originator, promoter, author', the person who makes something grow or brings it about. The word began with creation, not with command.
items.cn: auctor 意为「发起者、推动者、作者」，即使某物生长或促成其事的人。这个词从创造开始，而非从命令开始。

items.en: Auctoritas meant 'advice, influence, prestige, command'. Roman authority rested on recognized standing as much as on force, a nuance the modern adjective tends to flatten.
items.cn: auctoritas 意为「建议、影响、威望、命令」。罗马的权威既靠公认地位，也靠武力，现代形容词往往抹平这一细微差别。

items.en: English authority is recorded from the Middle Ages, first for a right to command and later for an expert source. The noun still carries both readings.
items.cn: 英语 authority 自中世纪起有书证，先指发令的权利，后指专家性来源。这个名词至今兼有这两种读法。

items.en: The suffix -arian marks a person or thing that adheres to a principle, as in egalitarian and vegetarian. Added to authority it names adherence to concentrated authority.
items.cn: 后缀 -arian 标出信奉某一原则的人或事物，如 egalitarian 与 vegetarian。加在 authority 上，它指对集中权威的信奉。

items.en: The adjective fixed as a technical term for non-democratic but not fully totalitarian systems in the twentieth century, and psychology applied it to personalities after 1950. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest technical citation is not fixed.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个形容词固定为指「非民主但未达完全极权」体制的术语；心理学在 1950 年之后把它用于人格。首见年代不确定：最早的技术性书证并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin auctor root or with a confusingly similar shape; group two holds adjectives for neighbouring kinds of concentrated rule.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 auctor 词根或外形近似到易混的词；第二组是描述相邻集中统治类型的形容词。

entries.definition: The right or power to command, or an expert body. Authoritarian is the adjective for a way of using that power.
entries.definitionCN: 指发令的权利或权力，或专家机构。authoritarian 是描述使用这种权力方式的形容词。

entries.definition: Trustworthy and expert, as in an authoritative account. It is often confused with authoritarian, but it praises reliability rather than obedience.
entries.definitionCN: 指可信且有专家根据，如权威性的记述。它常与 authoritarian 混淆，但它赞扬可靠性，而非要求服从。

entries.definition: The doctrine or regime; authoritarian is the adjective or the person who supports it.
entries.definitionCN: 指学说或政权；authoritarian 是形容词或支持者。

entries.definition: A person who writes or creates something, from the same Latin root. The word began with making, not with ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 指写作或创造某物的人，同出拉丁词根。这个词始于创造，而非统治。

entries.definition: From Greek authentikos 'original, genuine', not from Latin auctor. It means real or genuine and has no connection with authority.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊 authentikos「原本的、真正的」，并非拉丁 auctor。它意为真实、真品，与权威无关。

entries.definition: Relating to rule by one person with sole authority; it stresses the number of rulers, while authoritarian stresses the demand for obedience.
entries.definitionCN: 与一人独掌权威的统治相关；它强调统治者人数，而 authoritarian 强调要求服从。

entries.definition: Like a dictator: unchecked and often arbitrary. Authoritarian can describe a legal system with elections, so it is sometimes softer.
entries.definitionCN: 像独裁者一样：不受制约且往往任意。authoritarian 可描述带选举的法律制度，因此有时语气较缓。

entries.definition: Exercising power at a ruler's whim; the word judges the rule harshly, while authoritarian is a cooler analytical label.
entries.definitionCN: 按统治者心意行使权力；这个词严厉评判统治，而 authoritarian 是较冷静的分析标签。

entries.definition: Seeking control over every part of life, including private thought; it is a stronger claim than authoritarian, which can allow a private sphere.
entries.definitionCN: 试图控制生活的每一部分，包括私人思想；它比 authoritarian 是更强的断言，后者可允许私人领域存在。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin root, a real suffix of adherence and real social-science phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的表信奉后缀与真实的社会科学用语。

normal.en: Authority plus -arian: the ending means adherence, so the word names those who cling to concentrated authority.
normal.cn: authority 加 -arian：词尾意为信奉，因此这个词指紧抓集中权威的人。

normal.en: The family runs authority, authorize, authoritative, authoritarian, authoritarianism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 authority、authorize、authoritative、authoritarian、authoritarianism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: an authoritarian regime, authoritarian personality, authoritarian parenting.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：威权政权、威权人格、专制型教养。

normal.en: Do not confuse authoritative with authoritarian: one means reliable, the other means bossy.
normal.cn: 不要把 authoritative 与 authoritarian 混淆：一个意为可信，一个意为专横。

normal.en: The root began with growth and creation, not with command.
normal.cn: 这个词根最初表示生长与创造，而非命令。

abstract.en: Picture a door with a sign that says do as I say, and no handle on your side.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，挂着「照我说的做」的牌子，你这一侧没有门把手。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder where every rung is an approval stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，每一级都是一个审批印章。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the thermostat is locked behind glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，恒温器被锁在玻璃后面。

examples.en: The country moved from an authoritarian regime to a fragile democracy.
examples.cn: 这个国家从威权政权走向脆弱的民主。

examples.en: Authoritarian management drove away the most experienced staff.
examples.cn: 威权式管理赶走了最有经验的员工。

examples.en: The study measured authoritarian attitudes among first-year students.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了一年级学生的威权态度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「权威」加「信奉」：信奉集中权威、要求服从；这属构词说明，并非谐音联想

root: 拉丁 augere「增加、生长」（更早词根为重构形式）→ auctor「发起者、作者」→ auctoritas「建议、影响、命令」→ 英语 authority；加后缀 -arian（信奉……的，仿法语 autoritaire）构成 authoritarian（十九世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a way of holding power to a way of ranking values: obedience demanded, a regime, a believer, a parent, a boss, a personality, a culture and an ideology that prefers order to liberty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从握权方式走向价值排序：要求服从、政权、信奉者、父母、上司、人格、文化，以及把秩序置于自由之上的意识形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk with a sign reading do as I say, a pen for every approval, and a queue waiting outside the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子，牌子上写着「照我说的做」，每份批准都要用那支笔，门外排着等候的人。

branches.en: The demand for obedience and the ranking of order above liberty are one preference seen as habit and as doctrine.
branches.cn: 要求服从与把秩序置于自由之上，是同一偏好在习惯与教义两个层面的呈现。

branches.en: A regime is the demand written into law, with elections kept only as a façade.
branches.cn: 政权是把这一要求写进法律，选举只留作门面。

branches.en: A believer and the belief share one form, which is why the adjective can also name a person.
branches.cn: 信徒与信条共用同一个形式，因此这个形容词也能指人。

branches.en: The family and the university are the same authority at two sizes, one with children and one with colleagues.
branches.cn: 家庭与大学是同一权威的两种尺寸，一个面对孩子，一个面对同事。

branches.en: A boss and a personality are the same trait seen from outside and from inside.
branches.cn: 上司与人格是同一特质从外部与内部看到的两种样子。

intro.en: Authoritarian is a Latin noun of authority plus a suffix of adherence, so it reads as 'one who holds to concentrated authority'.
intro.cn: authoritarian 是表示权威的拉丁名词加表信奉的后缀，因此可读作「信奉集中权威者」。

latinIntro.en: Latin auctor and auctoritas supply the base; auctor comes from augere 'to increase', whose older Indo-European root is reconstructed rather than attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 auctor 与 auctoritas 提供基础；auctor 出自 augere「增加」，其更早的印欧词根是重构的，而非有书证的。

items.example: The root begins with growth, not with command.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根始于生长，而非命令。

items.example: The person-word names one who brings something about.
items.exampleCN: 这个指人的词指促成某事的人。

items.example: The abstract noun adds standing and weight to the person.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词在个人之上加上了地位与分量。

items.meaning: the right to command; an expert body
items.example: English took the noun in the Middle Ages.
items.exampleCN: 英语在中世纪借入这个名词。

items.example: The suffix marks adherence to a principle.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出对某一原则的信奉。

items.example: English formed the adjective in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十九世纪构成这个形容词。

items.example: A true friend of the word, often mistaken for the other.
items.exampleCN: 这是这个词真正的近亲，却常被误认作另一词。

items.example: The verb names the act of granting authority.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指授予权威的行为。

items.example: The oldest sense is creation, not rule.
items.exampleCN: 最古老的含义是创造，而非统治。

definition_zh: 威权主义；专制主义；要求服从的体制或倾向；家长式管理作风
definition_en: a political system or tendency that concentrates power and demands obedience rather than consent
core_image: 一座层层向上的审批阶梯，每一级都盖一个章，最上面只有一间盖章的屋子
scene: 地方报纸被要求先送审，学校里不准学生公开讨论校政，法院的判决常被上级改写。Scholars traced the rise of authoritarianism to the erosion of local courts.
sceneCN: 地方报纸被要求先送审，学校里不准学生公开讨论校政，法院的判决常被上级改写；句中这个词指「把权力集中于权威、要求服从而非同意的政治体制或倾向」（第 1 个义项：以集中权力与压制异议为核心特征的制度或思潮）。句意为学者把威权主义的兴起追溯到地方法院受到侵蚀。可辨识物件：送审稿件、上锁的布告栏、改过的判决书、审批章。

pos.zh: 威权主义；专制主义（不可数）
（某一具体的）威权体制（可数，指不同国家的实例时用复数）

senses.title: A political system
senses.definition: a system in which power is concentrated at the top and opposition is limited or managed
senses.definitionCN: 权力集中于上层、反对力量受限或被操控的制度
senses.example: Scholars traced the rise of authoritarianism to the erosion of local courts.
senses.exampleCN: 学者把威权主义的兴起追溯到地方法院受到侵蚀。
senses.why: The noun adds -ism to the adjective, turning a way of ruling into a named system that can rise, spread or fall.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在形容词后加 -ism，把一种统治方式变成可兴起、扩散或衰落的具名制度。

senses.title: An ideology
senses.definition: a set of beliefs that treats obedience and order as the highest political goods
senses.definitionCN: 把服从与秩序视为最高政治价值的一套信念
senses.example: Authoritarianism treats order as the highest good.
senses.exampleCN: 威权主义把秩序视为最高的善。
senses.why: Adding -ism also names a doctrine, so the same word can describe a regime and the ideas that defend it.
senses.whyCN: 加 -ism 也命名一种教义，因此同一个词既可描述政权，也可描述为它辩护的思想。

senses.title: The practice of demanding obedience
senses.definition: the habit, inside any group, of treating disagreement as insubordination
senses.definitionCN: 在任何团体内部把异议当作不服从的习惯
senses.example: The committee's authoritarianism showed in how it handled minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会的威权作风体现在它处理会议记录的方式上。
senses.why: The doctrine shrinks to a habit when no state is involved, and the same noun covers the habit.
senses.whyCN: 不涉及国家时，教义就缩小为习惯，而同一个名词也涵盖这种习惯。

senses.title: A personality disposition
senses.definition: a measurable preference for hierarchy, rigid rules and submission to strong leaders
senses.definitionCN: 对等级、僵化规则与服从强者的可测量偏好
senses.example: Psychologists measured authoritarianism with a questionnaire.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学家用问卷测量威权主义倾向。
senses.why: Twentieth-century psychology made the political noun into a scale, which is why it appears in survey research.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪心理学把这个政治名词变成量表，因此它出现在调查研究里。

senses.title: Organizational management
senses.definition: a style of running an institution through one-way orders and layered approvals
senses.definitionCN: 靠单向命令与层层审批运行机构的方式
senses.example: The firm's authoritarianism slowed every decision.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的威权作风让每个决定都变慢。
senses.why: Institutions reproduce the state in miniature, so the political noun describes an office hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 机构是国家的缩小复制，因此这个政治名词可描述办公室层级。

senses.title: A parenting pattern
senses.definition: raising children with strict rules, punishment and little explanation
senses.definitionCN: 以严格规则、惩罚与极少解释养育孩子
senses.example: Strict rules without explanation amount to authoritarianism.
senses.exampleCN: 立规矩却不解释，就构成威权式教养。
senses.why: The family is the smallest polity, and the noun follows the pattern wherever authority is unchecked.
senses.whyCN: 家庭是最小的政治体，这个词随不受制约的权威走到哪里就跟到哪里。

senses.title: Digital authoritarianism
senses.definition: the use of surveillance, data and network control to keep a population compliant
senses.definitionCN: 利用监控、数据与网络控制使民众顺从
senses.example: Digital authoritarianism uses surveillance to keep power.
senses.exampleCN: 数字威权主义用监控维持权力。
senses.why: New tools give old concentrated power a new form, so a new compound is built from the old noun.
senses.whyCN: 新工具给旧的集中权力一个新形式，因此用旧名词造出新复合词。

senses.title: A drift inside a democracy
senses.definition: the gradual weakening of checks and competition inside elected institutions
senses.definitionCN: 民选机构内部制衡与竞争的逐步削弱
senses.example: Scholars warn of authoritarianism inside elected institutions.
senses.exampleCN: 学者警告民选机构内部存在威权化倾向。
senses.why: The concept is comparative rather than binary, so a democracy can be measured for authoritarian drift.
senses.whyCN: 这个概念是比较性的，而非二元的，因此可以测量一个民主国家的威权漂移。

intro.en: Authoritarianism is authoritarian plus -ism. The adjective was formed in the nineteenth century from authority, and the noun fixed as a political-science label in the twentieth.
intro.cn: authoritarianism 是 authoritarian 加 -ism。形容词在十九世纪由 authority 构成，名词在二十世纪固定为政治学标签。

items.en: Auctoritas meant 'influence, advice, command'. Roman authority rested on recognized standing as much as on force, a nuance that the modern noun tends to drop.
items.cn: auctoritas 意为「影响、建议、命令」。罗马的权威既靠公认地位，也靠武力，现代名词往往丢掉这一细微差别。

items.en: Auctor 'originator' came from augere 'to increase'. The family began with growth and creation rather than with command, and the older Indo-European root is reconstructed.
items.cn: auctor「发起者」出自 augere「增加」。这个词族始于生长与创造，而非命令；更早的印欧词根是重构形式。

items.en: English authority is recorded from the Middle Ages and already carried both 'right to command' and 'expert source'. The noun still holds both readings.
items.cn: 英语 authority 自中世纪起有书证，已同时带有「发令权」与「专家性来源」两义。这个名词至今保留两种读法。

items.en: The ending -arian marks adherence to a principle, and -ism then turns that adherence into a named system of belief.
items.cn: 词尾 -arian 标出对某一原则的信奉，-ism 再把这种信奉变成具名的信念体系。

items.en: Authoritarian was formed in the nineteenth century, modelled partly on French autoritaire. Dates are approximate.
items.cn: authoritarian 在十九世纪构成，部分仿照法语 autoritaire。年代为约数。

items.en: The noun became a standard term in comparative politics and psychology by the mid-twentieth century, and digital and electoral compounds followed. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest technical citation is not fixed.
items.cn: 到二十世纪中期，这个名词成为比较政治学与心理学的标准术语，数字与选举类复合词随后出现。首见年代不确定：最早的技术性书证并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same authority family or with a nearly identical shape; group two holds names for neighbouring systems of concentrated rule.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 authority 词族或外形极近的词；第二组是描述相邻集中统治体系的名称。

entries.definition: The adjective describing the system, or the person who supports it. Authoritarianism is the system or doctrine itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述该体制的形容词，或支持者。authoritarianism 是体制或学说本身。

entries.definition: The right to command or an expert body; it can exist inside a democracy and does not by itself mean authoritarianism.
entries.definitionCN: 指发令权或专家机构；它可存在于民主制度内部，本身并不等于威权主义。

entries.definition: Trustworthy and expert, as in an authoritative study. The similarity in spelling hides a completely different judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 指可信且有专家根据，如权威性研究。拼写相似掩盖了完全不同的评价。

entries.definition: A writer or originator, from the same root. Creation is the oldest sense of the family, not command.
entries.definitionCN: 指作者或发起者，同出该词根。创造才是这个词族最古老的含义，而非命令。

entries.definition: From Greek authentikos 'genuine', with no link to Latin auctor. It means real, not authoritative.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊 authentikos「真正的」，与拉丁 auctor 无关。它意为真实，而非权威。

entries.definition: Rule by one person with unrestricted power; it stresses the number of rulers, while authoritarianism stresses the demand for obedience.
entries.definitionCN: 由一人掌握不受限制的权力；它强调统治者人数，而 authoritarianism 强调要求服从。

entries.definition: Absolute rule at a ruler's whim; it stresses caprice, while authoritarianism can be a bureaucratic system without a single tyrant.
entries.definitionCN: 按统治者心意行使的绝对统治；它强调任意性，而 authoritarianism 可以是没有单一暴君的官僚体系。

entries.definition: Rule by an unchecked dictator; it usually names a person's regime, while authoritarianism can describe a whole political culture.
entries.definitionCN: 不受制约的独裁者统治；它通常指个人的政权，而 authoritarianism 可描述整片政治文化。

entries.definition: A system that seeks control over private life and thought as well; it is a stronger and more specific claim than authoritarianism.
entries.definitionCN: 试图连私人生活与思想一并控制的制度；它比 authoritarianism 是更强、更具体的断言。

entries.definition: Opposition to liberal rights and open competition; it overlaps with authoritarianism but can exist inside a formally democratic system.
entries.definitionCN: 反对自由权利与公开竞争；它与 authoritarianism 有交集，却可存在于形式上民主的制度中。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin root, two real suffixes and real comparative-politics phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、两个真实后缀与真实的比较政治学用语。

normal.en: Authority plus -arian plus -ism: adherence to concentrated authority becomes a named system.
normal.cn: authority 加 -arian 再加 -ism：对集中权威的信奉变成一套具名制度。

normal.en: The family runs authority, authoritarian, authoritarianism, authoritative, authorize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 authority、authoritarian、authoritarianism、authoritative、authorize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: the rise of authoritarianism, digital authoritarianism, electoral authoritarianism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：威权主义的兴起、数字威权主义、选举式威权主义。

normal.en: The word can be comparative: a democracy can show authoritarian drift without becoming a dictatorship.
normal.cn: 这个词可以作比较用：民主国家可能出现威权漂移，却未变成独裁。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with authoritative, which praises reliability rather than obedience.
normal.cn: 不要把它与 authoritative 混淆，后者称赞可靠性，而非服从。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase where every step is a stamp and the top room has only the stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一座阶梯，每一级都是一个印章，最上面的屋子里只有那枚印章。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat locked behind glass while the room grows hot.
abstract.cn: 想象恒温器被锁在玻璃后，屋子却越来越热。

abstract.en: Picture a web that catches opinions before they reach the square.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网，在意见到达广场之前就把它们兜住。

examples.en: Comparativists measure authoritarianism by the independence of courts.
examples.cn: 比较政治学者用法院的独立性来衡量威权主义。

examples.en: Digital authoritarianism spreads faster than the laws that restrain it.
examples.cn: 数字威权主义传播得比约束它的法律更快。

examples.en: The factory's authoritarianism ended when the night shift organised.
examples.cn: 夜班工人组织起来后，这家工厂的威权作风终结了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「权威」加「信奉」再加「主义」：把服从权威当成最高原则；这属构词说明，并非谐音联想

root: 拉丁 augere「增加、生长」（更早词根为重构形式）→ auctor「发起者」→ auctoritas「影响、命令、权威」→ 英语 authority；加 -arian（信奉……的）构成 authoritarian，再加 -ism（主义）构成 authoritarianism（十九至二十世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one principle from a state to a family: a regime, a doctrine, a habit, a personality, a management style, a parenting pattern, a digital form and a drift inside democracies.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个原则从国家走到家庭：政权、教义、习惯、人格、管理作风、教养模式、数字形态，以及民主内部的漂移。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a staircase of approvals, each step stamping the same page, with a small room at the top holding the only stamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座审批阶梯，每一级都在同一页上盖章，最顶端的小屋里放着唯一的那枚印章。

branches.en: A regime and a drift are the same concentration measured at full strength and at low strength.
branches.cn: 政权与漂移是同一集中度的满格与低格。

branches.en: The ideology supplies the reasons that the regime uses to justify itself.
branches.cn: 意识形态提供政权用来为自己辩护的理由。

branches.en: A habit of demanding obedience and a parenting pattern are the same demand at home and at work.
branches.cn: 要求服从的习惯与教养模式，是同一要求在家庭与工作中的两种场景。

branches.en: A personality is the principle installed inside one person, where it needs no institution.
branches.cn: 人格是安装在一个个体内部的这一原则，在那里它不需要制度。

branches.en: Management and surveillance are the same control with a clipboard and with a camera.
branches.cn: 管理与监控是同一控制的两种工具：一个用夹板，一个用摄像头。

intro.en: Authoritarianism stacks two endings on a Latin noun of authority: one marks adherence, the other turns that adherence into a named system.
intro.cn: authoritarianism 在表示权威的拉丁名词上叠了两个词尾：一个标出信奉，另一个把信奉变成具名体系。

latinIntro.en: Latin auctor and auctoritas supply the base; auctor comes from augere 'to increase', whose older Indo-European root is reconstructed rather than attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 auctor 与 auctoritas 提供基础；auctor 出自 augere「增加」，其更早的印欧词根是重构的，而非有书证的。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根始于生长，而非命令。

items.exampleCN: 这个指人的词指促成某事的人。

items.example: The abstract noun turns standing into a right to be obeyed.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词把地位变成被服从的权利。

items.example: English took the noun in the Middle Ages.
items.exampleCN: 英语在中世纪借入这个名词。

items.example: The suffix marks adherence.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出信奉。

items.example: The adjective was formed in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在十九世纪构成。

items.structure: -ismus (Greek and Latin suffix, system or doctrine)
items.example: The suffix turns an attitude into a named system.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把态度变成具名体系。

items.example: The whole word names a doctrine and a regime at once.
items.exampleCN: 整词同时命名教义与政权。

items.example: A near neighbour that praises reliability, not obedience.
items.exampleCN: 一个近亲，赞扬可靠性而非服从。
